headline: This year starts with a new creation
prayer: Jesus, I'm here on day one, and I want a real new start, not just a fresh calendar. You make things new, so start with me. Show me what needs to die, and give me the guts to let it go.
reading: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.
in_jesus: In Christ you are a new creation. Jesus died and rose so the old record is closed and a new life is yours. You don't earn the fresh start. He already paid for it.
reflect: What is one thing from your old life you keep picking back up, and why?
act: Name it out loud before you leave the house today. Then text one brother you trust and tell him you're done carrying it.

headline: His mercy showed up before you did
prayer: Father, Your mercy was here before I woke up. I blew it yesterday and You didn't quit on me. Because of Jesus, I don't have to wallow in it. Make me faithful with this day.
reading: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
in_jesus: Jesus carried yesterday's failure to the cross, so mercy isn't a mood God happens to be in. It is bought and settled. His faithfulness holds when yours doesn't.
reflect: Are you still living under yesterday's failure when God has already moved on?
act: Before noon, finish the one thing you would have quit on yesterday.

headline: You were made for work already prepared
prayer: Father, You built me on purpose and for a purpose. Holy Spirit, open my eyes to the good work You laid out for me today, and don't let me walk past it because I'm busy or lazy. I ask it in Jesus' name.
reading: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.
in_jesus: You are created in Christ Jesus. His work on the cross makes you God's workmanship, so the good works flow from what he did, not from you proving yourself.
reflect: You weren't saved to sit. What good work is already in front of you?
act: Ask the Spirit to show you one need at work or at home. Meet it before 5 p.m., quietly, with no credit.

headline: Stop driving by the rearview mirror
prayer: Lord, I keep replaying old wins, old wounds, and old failures. Jesus, turn my head forward. Show me the road You're cutting through my wilderness right now, and help me trust it before I can see it.
reading: Remember not the former things, nor consider the things of old. Behold, I am doing a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
in_jesus: Jesus is the new thing God promised. At the cross and the empty tomb he opened a way through the wilderness, and he goes ahead of you into this year.
reflect: What old thing do you replay most, and what would change if you gave it to God?
act: Tonight, write one sentence naming a new thing God is doing in you. Read it to your wife or a brother.

headline: The old you died with Christ
prayer: Jesus, You took the old me to Your cross. Don't let me dig him back up. Live through my hands, my mouth, and my choices today, because I can't do this alone. Less of me. More of You.
reading: I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
in_jesus: Christ loved you and gave himself for you. He doesn't just forgive the old man, he lives in you now, so this new life runs on his strength, not yours.
reflect: Where are you still running your life like it belongs to you?
act: Pick one decision today, a purchase, a reply, or a word to your kids. Ask what it looks like to let Christ lead it, then do that.

headline: God's verdict on you is wonderful
prayer: Father, I've believed lies about who I am. Some I told myself. Some other people handed me. Silence them with Your truth today. Through Jesus, I'm Yours, and You made me on purpose, so teach me to believe it.
reading: I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it very well.
in_jesus: Jesus looked at broken men and called them his own. He came to seek and save the lost, and his voice outweighs every lie you have believed about yourself.
reflect: What lie do you believe about yourself that God never said?
act: Write that lie on paper and cross it out. Write Psalm 139:14 beside it and keep it in your wallet or truck today.

headline: No condemnation. Not one ounce.
prayer: Lord, I'm tired of carrying guilt You already paid for. Jesus took the condemnation, so help me take the conviction and move. Where I need to change, change me. Where I need to stop punishing myself, make me stop.
reading: There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
in_jesus: At the cross Jesus took the full condemnation sin deserves. For everyone in Christ the verdict is settled, so conviction can lead you to change without crushing you.
reflect: Conviction says change. Condemnation says you're worthless. Which voice do you hear when you fail?
act: Today, tell one coworker or friend who is carrying guilt that Jesus took it for him. Share one thing Jesus forgave you for.

headline: You are a son, not a hired hand
prayer: Father, remind me whose I am. Not a hired hand. Not a project. A son. Because of Jesus, let that settle deep into my bones today so I stop working for approval I already have.
reading: See what kind of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God; and so we are. The reason why the world does not know us is that it did not know him.
in_jesus: Jesus made you a child of God through his death and resurrection. The Father's love for you doesn't rise and fall with your performance, because it rests on his Son.
reflect: Do you live like a son or like a hired hand trying to earn his keep?
act: Before work, stand in your kitchen or driveway for five minutes and thank the Father for calling you his through Jesus.

headline: Nothing today catches God off guard
prayer: Father, You wrote every one of my days before I lived one. Jesus, You told me not to worry, so I'm handing You the worries that kept me up. You hold today. I'll walk it.
reading: Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me, when as yet there was none of them.
in_jesus: Jesus tells you not to be anxious because your Father knows what you need. The same Christ who went to the cross on God's set plan holds every hour of your day.
reflect: What are you anxious about that God already saw coming?
act: Write down the worry that kept you up and pray over it right now. Pray again each time it shows up today.

headline: God replaces stone hearts with living ones
prayer: Lord, something in me has gone hard toward my wife, my kids, or You. I can't fix it myself. Holy Spirit, take out the stone and give me a heart that feels again. I ask it in Jesus' name.
reading: And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
in_jesus: Jesus gave his own life so the Spirit could be poured out and dead hearts could be made alive. The heart he gives feels, forgives, and follows.
reflect: Where has your heart gone cold: your wife, your kids, or God?
act: Tonight, do one warm thing for the person you've been cold toward. Ask the Spirit for the first words, then say them.

headline: You haven't arrived. Press on anyway.
prayer: Jesus, I haven't arrived, and I'm done pretending I have. You already took hold of me. Keep my eyes on You and my feet moving, and give me one clear next step today, and the grit to take it.
reading: Brothers, I do not consider that I have made it my own. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.
in_jesus: Paul presses on because Christ Jesus first took hold of him. Jesus finished the work on the cross, so your progress is a response to him, not a way to earn him.
reflect: Paul said he hadn't arrived either. What is your next step forward?
act: Write one spiritual goal for this year on a card and tape it where you'll see it every morning. Make it a step toward Jesus, not a performance target.

headline: Your old life is dead and buried
prayer: Father, my old life is dead and my real life is hidden with Christ in You. Keep me there. When the old habits call my name today, remind me that man is gone because of Jesus.
reading: For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
in_jesus: You died with Christ, and now your life is hidden with him in God. Jesus holds it secure at the Father's right hand, where no old habit can reach it.
reflect: If your old self is dead, why do you keep visiting the grave?
act: Pick one habit that belongs to the old you. Delete the app, toss the stash, or cancel the subscription before lunch.

headline: You carry God's image. So does he.
prayer: Creator God, You made me a man in Your image, and Jesus is the perfect image of You. Help me carry it with honor today, and help me see Your image in everyone I deal with, especially the hard ones.
reading: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.
in_jesus: Christ is the image of the invisible God, and he came to restore the image sin has marred in us. He died for the difficult people too.
reflect: You carry God's image, and so does the man who irritates you. How does that change how you treat him?
act: Pick the hardest person you'll deal with today. Greet him by name and listen without interrupting.

headline: Cut off from Jesus, you can do nothing
prayer: Jesus, You said apart from You I can do nothing, and I keep trying to prove You wrong. Keep me connected today. In my work, my home, and my training, let me draw strength from You, not caffeine and willpower.
reading: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
in_jesus: Jesus is the true vine, and he gives his life to every branch that stays in him. Fruit isn't produced by your grit. It grows from his life flowing through you.
reflect: Where are you trying to bear fruit on your own strength?
act: Invite a coworker or neighbor who doesn't know Jesus to coffee this week. Pray before you ask, then tell him one way Jesus has held you up.

headline: Scarlet sins. White as snow.
prayer: Lord, You invite me to reason with You, stains and all, so I'm bringing all of it. Wash me clean through the blood of Jesus, and help me walk like a man who has been washed.
reading: Come now, let us reason together, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
in_jesus: The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin. What looks like scarlet to you, he makes white as snow. No sin is bigger than his cross.
reflect: Is there a sin you think is too big for God to clean?
act: Name that sin to God out loud, in the truck or the shower. Then say, "Jesus paid for this," and receive his forgiveness.

headline: Called out of darkness into his light
prayer: Father, You chose me and called me out of the dark, and I didn't earn it. Help me live like a chosen man through Jesus today, and let someone see Your light in how I live.
reading: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
in_jesus: Jesus is the light of the world, and he brought you out of darkness at the cost of his life. Your story points people to him, not to you.
reflect: You were called out of the dark. Does your life point anyone toward the light?
act: Tell one person today what Jesus has done for you. Keep it to two sentences and say it face to face.

headline: East to west. That's how far.
prayer: Father, You took my sin as far as the east is from the west, and I couldn't move it an inch. Thank You for Jesus. Holy Spirit, when old shame shows up today, help me leave it where he put it.
reading: As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us.
in_jesus: Jesus bore your sin on the cross and carried it away. The distance between you and your guilt is as wide as east from west, and he is the one who closed the gap.
reflect: God doesn't dig up what he buried. Why do you?
act: When an old sin comes to mind today, ask the Spirit for help, say out loud, "Jesus carried that," and get back to work.

headline: Let Scripture shape you, not your feed
prayer: Lord, the world has shaped my thinking more than You have. Renew my mind through Christ. Rewire what I believe, what I want, and what I feed on, until I think like Your Word and not like my feed.
reading: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect.
in_jesus: Jesus says his words are spirit and life. In Christ you are given a new mind to be renewed, and he is the one doing the transforming, not your willpower.
reflect: What shapes your thinking more, your phone or God's Word?
act: Swap 15 minutes of scrolling this morning for 15 minutes in one of the Gospels. Read until you see Jesus do something.

headline: God sings over you. Let him.
prayer: God, my mind runs hot with bills, work, and family all at once. Quiet me with Your love in Christ. Let me hear You rejoicing over me, even on a day I don't feel like much.
reading: The LORD your God is in your midst, a mighty one who will save; he will rejoice over you with gladness; he will quiet you by his love; he will exult over you with loud singing.
in_jesus: Jesus said, "Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." The Father's gladness over you is secured by the Son.
reflect: God sings over you. When did you last let yourself believe that?
act: Take ten quiet minutes before bed with your phone in another room. Read Zephaniah 3:17 and sit with it.

headline: You're a son by gift, not effort
prayer: Jesus, I received You once, and I receive You again today, not as a guest but as Lord. Thank You for making me a son of God. Help me stop performing and start living from that.
reading: But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God.
in_jesus: Jesus gives the right to become children of God to all who receive him. You didn't earn it, and you can't lose it by missing a day.
reflect: Your standing with God was given, not earned. Where are you still trying to earn it?
act: Obey him today out of gratitude, not fear. Pick one thing you've put off and do it before lunch, telling Jesus why.

headline: He finishes what he starts in you
prayer: Lord, You started something in me, and You don't quit halfway. Finish it through Jesus, who started it. Give me patience with the process and with myself, and keep me cooperating instead of fighting You.
reading: And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ.
in_jesus: Jesus said, "It is finished," and the Father will complete his work in you by the day of Christ Jesus. He doesn't leave projects half done.
reflect: You're not finished, and neither is God. Where do you need patience with yourself?
act: Find a younger man at church or work. Tell him one way God has grown you this past year, and ask how you can pray for him.

headline: Ask God for a clean heart
prayer: God, create a clean heart in me. Not a patched one. A new one. Renew a steady spirit so I don't crack the next time pressure or temptation hits. I ask it because Jesus makes me clean.
reading: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
in_jesus: David asked for a clean heart, and Jesus Christ is the answer. His blood cleanses us, and he gives the Spirit who renews us from the inside.
reflect: David prayed this after his worst failure. What is yours?
act: Pray Psalm 51:10 three times today, at breakfast, lunch, and bedtime. Set the phone alarms now.

headline: Bought back by blood. Paid in full.
prayer: Jesus, You paid what I owed with Your own blood, and I can't repay it. Let that grace make me generous today, especially toward the people who owe me, and humble about how much I was forgiven.
reading: In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace.
in_jesus: Redemption cost Jesus his blood. He paid the full price to buy you back, and he forgave you while you were still a sinner.
reflect: Redemption means bought back. What did it cost Jesus to buy you back?
act: Forgive one person who owes you. Tell him so by call or text today, and mean it.

headline: Saved from something, and for something
prayer: Lord, You saved me for something, not just from something. Holy Spirit, show me my calling and make me willing, even if it costs me comfort. I belong to Jesus, so lead me and make it clear.
reading: Who saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works but because of his own purpose and grace, which he gave us in Christ Jesus before the ages began.
in_jesus: Christ Jesus gave you grace before time began, and he says, "As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you." Your calling rests on his grace, not your record.
reflect: You're saved for something, not just from something. What is it?
act: Ask the Spirit, "What do you want me doing with my life?" Spend ten minutes listening, then tell your wife or a brother what you sensed.

headline: Christ freed you. Quit going back.
prayer: God, You set me free, and I keep wandering back to the chains. Some I've gotten comfortable with. Break them through Jesus, who already won my freedom, and give me the backbone to stand firm and not go back.
reading: For freedom Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
in_jesus: Jesus said, "If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." Christ didn't loosen the chains. He broke them at the cross.
reflect: What are you free from that you keep walking back to?
act: Remove one access point to that thing before tonight. Delete it, block it, or throw it out, and tell a brother you did.

headline: God threw your sin in the sea
prayer: Father, You tread my sin underfoot and throw it in the deepest sea, and I don't deserve that compassion. Thank You for Jesus. Let me show a little of that same compassion to someone who needs it today.
reading: He will again have compassion on us; he will tread our iniquities underfoot. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.
in_jesus: The sin God casts into the sea was laid on Jesus at the cross. He bore the penalty, so the Father's compassion toward you is not cheap, and it is complete.
reflect: God threw it in the sea. Why do you keep fishing it out?
act: Text a brother today and tell him how God forgave you. Be specific about the sin.

headline: Deep roots hold when storms hit
prayer: Jesus, root me deep in You. Not a shallow faith that blows over in the first storm. Build me up slow and strong, one ordinary day at a time, and let thankfulness spill out of me today.
reading: Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
in_jesus: You received Christ Jesus the Lord, and he is the soil. He holds you fast, so your roots grow in his faithfulness, not in your streak of good days.
reflect: Roots grow in the dark, slowly, daily. Are yours deep enough to hold in a storm?
act: Pick a set time and place for Scripture this week and put it on your calendar now. Same time, same chair, every day.

headline: God moves among men who are ready
prayer: Lord, set me apart for You today. Show me what I need to clear out so I'm ready. Jesus made me holy by his sacrifice, so I want to be a man You can work through.
reading: Then Joshua said to the people, “Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you.”
in_jesus: Jesus Christ sets you apart. By his one offering he has made perfect those who are being sanctified, so you consecrate yourself because he already claimed you, not to earn him.
reflect: God moves among men who are ready. What do you need to clear out to be ready?
act: Invite one man who doesn't know Jesus to the next Forged in Faith Saturday. First clear one thing from your phone or schedule so you can follow up.

headline: Walk in the power of the empty tomb
prayer: Jesus, You walked out of the grave, and You raised me with You. Help me walk in new life today. Not just feel it. Walk it, one step at a time, even when it's the hard step.
reading: We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.
in_jesus: Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, and you were united with him. His resurrection is not just history. It is the power behind your walk.
reflect: New life is a walk, not a feeling. What does your walk look like this week?
act: Take one step today you'd only take if you believed you were really new. Apologize first, speak up, or start the hard thing.

headline: Drop the weight. Run the race.
prayer: God, I'm carrying weight I don't need. Some of it is sin, and some of it is just clutter. Show me what to drop, and keep my eyes on Jesus so I have the endurance to run.
reading: Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us.
in_jesus: Jesus is the founder and perfecter of our faith. He endured the cross, despising its shame, and now sits at God's right hand, so you run toward him and never alone.
reflect: Not every weight is sin. Some just slow you down. What is slowing you down?
act: Drop one thing by this weekend that is costing you time with God or your family. Tell your wife what it is.

headline: Commit your whole year to him
prayer: Lord, I commit this year to You, all of it, not just Sundays. Work, marriage, kids, health, calendar. Holy Spirit, help me follow where You lead. Jesus, I trust You to do what only You can do.
reading: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in him, and he will act.
in_jesus: Christ is Lord over every part of your year, and he is faithful to act. He gave himself to the Father's will at the cross, so you can commit your way to him.
reflect: A month in, have you committed your way, or just your Sundays?
act: Review the goal you wrote on January 11. Ask the Spirit to adjust it, pray it over with Jesus as the reason, and share the update with a brother.

headline: Love her first, right after Christ
prayer: Jesus, You gave Yourself up for Your bride and put her first. Forgive me for handing my wife leftovers of my time and attention. Let my calendar and my choices say what my mouth claims about her.
reading: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.
in_jesus: Christ loved the church while she was still failing him, and he paid for her with his own life. His love came first. Yours is only a response.
reflect: If your marriage comes right after Christ in your priorities, does your calendar show it?
act: Tell your wife in plain words today that she comes first after God. Say it before lunch.

headline: Love is a decision, not a mood
prayer: Lord Jesus, I don't always feel it, but You loved me when I gave You nothing to feel. Make love something I do every morning, not something I wait on. Move me to act before my mood catches up.
reading: Little children, let us not love in word or talk but in deed and in truth.
in_jesus: Jesus did not wait to feel like laying down his life. He chose the cross for people who had not earned it, and he still loves you in deed and in truth.
reflect: Where have you been waiting to feel loving before you act loving?
act: Before 9 a.m., wash her coffee cup, fill her tank, or handle one chore she hates. Do it whether you feel like it or not.

headline: Your log comes out first
prayer: Father, I spend more energy fixing her than letting You fix me. Through Jesus, who took my judgment on himself, turn my eyes to the log in my own eye. Holy Spirit, help me actually do it today.
reading: You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.
in_jesus: Christ bore your sin so you can face it without hiding. You can name your own failures safely, because he already carried them to the cross.
reflect: What is one thing you keep asking her to change that God is asking you to change first?
act: Drop one complaint about her today. Tell her one thing you own about yourself, and ask the Spirit for the nerve to do it.

headline: Study her like she's worth knowing
prayer: Lord, I've stopped paying attention to the woman I promised my life to. Because Jesus knows me fully and still stays, teach me to know her the same way. Show me what I've quit noticing.
reading: The purpose in a man’s heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
in_jesus: Jesus knows every hidden thing in you and still calls you friend. That is the kind of attention he models for a husband.
reflect: Could you name her three biggest dreams and her three biggest fears right now?
act: Ask her one question you have never asked her. Write down the answer tonight.

headline: Serve her before she asks
prayer: Jesus, You came to serve, and I usually come to be served. You gave Your life as a ransom for me. Make me a husband who spots the need and moves before she has to ask.
reading: For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
in_jesus: Christ, the Son of Man, did not come to be served. He gave his life as a ransom for many, and that includes you.
reflect: What is one thing she loves that you could make happen for her today?
act: Pick one thing she loves and make it happen today. Do not wait for her to ask, and do not mention it afterward.

headline: Where your mind goes, you follow
prayer: Lord, what I dwell on, I move toward. Christ has made me his own, so train my mind to land on what I love about her and not on what bugs me. Fix my eyes where they belong.
reading: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence, if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
in_jesus: Everything true, lovely, and honorable is found in Christ. As he renews your mind, you start seeing your wife the way he sees her.
reflect: When you think about your wife today, where does your mind go first?
act: Write down five things you love about her. Read them in the car before you walk in the door tonight.

headline: Her differences are God's design
prayer: Father, You made her different on purpose. Through Jesus, who makes us one, help me see her differences as gifts and not as things to correct. Forgive me for treating them as flaws, and give me words to thank her.
reading: Then the LORD God said, “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him.”
in_jesus: Christ makes two different people one in him. Your wife's differences are not a problem he failed to solve. They are part of his plan for you.
reflect: Which of her differences have you been treating as wrong instead of as a gift?
act: Thank her for one way she is different from you that makes your life better. Then ask a coworker how his marriage is going, and tell him one thing Jesus is changing in yours.

headline: Winning the argument loses the marriage
prayer: Lord, when we argue I want to win. Jesus, You answered insults with silence and mercy. Give me a soft answer when I want a sharp one, and show me that if one of us wins, we both lose.
reading: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
in_jesus: When Jesus was reviled, he did not revile in return. He entrusted himself to the Father and bore your sins, and he gives you a gentler way to fight.
reflect: In your last argument, were you fighting for the marriage or for the win?
act: In your next disagreement, say out loud, "We're on the same team." Then lower your voice.

headline: Anger does not get to run your house
prayer: Holy Spirit, when I'm angry she still needs a husband who leads, loves, and serves. Jesus, You had every right to rage and chose the cross. Hold my temper so my emotions don't run our house.
reading: Whoever is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city.
in_jesus: Jesus ruled his spirit all the way to the cross. He is stronger than your anger, and his Spirit is at work in you to produce self-control.
reflect: Does she like the man you are when you're mad?
act: The next time anger rises, stop for ten seconds. Then do one small act of service for her instead of speaking.

headline: Step out of your comfort zone for her
prayer: Jesus, You stepped out of heaven for me. Give me a fraction of that humility. Holy Spirit, move me out of my comfort zone for her, so I do what she loves just because I love her.
reading: Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves. Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.
in_jesus: Christ did not cling to his place with the Father. He emptied himself and became a servant for you. His humility is the pattern and the power here.
reflect: What does she love doing that you have quietly avoided for years?
act: Pick one thing she loves to do, put it on the calendar this week, and do it with her gladly. Ask the Spirit to help you mean it.

headline: Listen to understand, not to answer
prayer: Lord, I listen to answer. Jesus, You listen to me every time I pray and never check the clock. Teach me to hear her words and read her face before I reply, and to stay quiet until she's done.
reading: Know this, my beloved brothers: let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
in_jesus: Christ hears you at any hour. He is the Word made flesh, and he draws near to you before you finish speaking.
reflect: When she talks, are you listening or loading your reply?
act: Tonight, let her finish completely. Then repeat back what you heard before you say a word of your own.

headline: Guard your heart, honor her publicly
prayer: Father, guard my heart and our marriage. Jesus, You are the guard I can't be for myself. Make me deliberate about what I let near this marriage, and quick to speak well of my wife to everyone around me.
reading: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
in_jesus: Christ is the keeper of your heart. You cannot guard it alone, and he does not ask you to. He holds you when you can't hold yourself.
reflect: Who heard you talk about your wife this week, and what did they hear?
act: Bring her up by name today, with praise, in a conversation with a friend or coworker.

headline: Stop keeping score. Go first.
prayer: Lord, I keep score. Free me from it. Jesus, You gave first and never sent me an invoice. Let me out-give her on purpose, and start a cycle of love in our home that doesn't quit.
reading: Give, and it will be given to you. Good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, will be put into your lap. For with the measure you use it will be measured back to you.
in_jesus: Christ gave first. While you were still a sinner he died for you, and he did not wait for you to pay him back.
reflect: Where are you waiting for her to go first?
act: Go first today. Give her something she doesn't expect, and do not ask for anything back.

headline: Affection that asks for nothing
prayer: Lord Jesus, You love Your people with a love that asks nothing back. On a day built for romance, make my affection warm, plain, and free of strings. Let her see You in how I love her.
reading: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me!
in_jesus: Christ delights in his bride and loves her without conditions. Jesus gave himself freely, and your love for your wife can be a picture of that.
reflect: Is your affection a gift to her or a request for something?
act: Kiss her and say "I love you" before you leave and when you walk in tonight. Then text a younger married man at church and offer to pray for his marriage this week.

headline: Fill up on Christ, then pour out
prayer: Jesus, I can't love her well if I'm not loving You first. Fill me so I have something to pour out. I'm never more like You than when I give and serve, so keep me close to You today.
reading: And he said to him, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment.”
in_jesus: Jesus is the first and greatest commandment kept perfectly, on your behalf. Because of him you are loved before you love, and that is where your love for her starts.
reflect: Is your time with God feeding your marriage or competing with it?
act: Give Christ ten minutes before you see her today, in the Word and in prayer. Then ask him how to love her.

headline: Let everyone see she comes first
prayer: Lord, make it obvious to everyone around me that she comes first, after You. Jesus, You honored Your bride publicly at the cross. Let my words and my choices do the same for mine, in front of anyone watching.
reading: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her.
in_jesus: Christ does not hide his love for his church. He declared it in front of everyone on the cross, and he presents her to himself in splendor.
reflect: Would your kids, friends, and coworkers say she comes first?
act: Praise your wife by name in front of someone else today.

headline: Overlook what doesn't matter
prayer: Father, give me the wisdom to overlook what doesn't matter. Jesus, You overlooked my offenses and carried what I couldn't. Holy Spirit, help me slow down and ask the right questions before I react when she bugs me.
reading: Good sense makes one slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
in_jesus: Christ covered your offenses with his blood instead of counting them against you. His patience with you is how you learn patience with her.
reflect: When something she does bugs you, is it hurting her, is it truly hurting you, or is it just something you don't like? Can you let it go?
act: Run the next thing that bugs you through three questions: Is it hurting her? Is it truly hurting me? Is it against God's law in our marriage? If not, let it go.

headline: Make a covenant with your eyes
prayer: Lord, I make a covenant with my eyes today. Jesus, You were tempted in every way and never sinned, so You know my weakness. Keep me from conversations or glances that don't belong to my wife.
reading: I have made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a virgin?
in_jesus: Jesus was tempted as you are, yet without sin. He sympathizes with your weakness and offers mercy and grace when you fail and when you run to him.
reflect: When you travel or you're away from her, what are your rules?
act: Set one rule for how you talk with women on the road. Tell your wife what it is tonight.

headline: Keep her friendship circle shared
prayer: Father, I don't want even a hint of anything that pulls my heart from her. Because Christ has made me clean, keep my friendships with women inside our marriage and not apart from it. Show me anything I'm hiding or excusing.
reading: But sexual immorality and all impurity or covetousness must not even be named among you, as is proper among saints.
in_jesus: Christ cleanses you from all unrighteousness. In him you are a new man, so you can live in the open and have nothing to hide.
reflect: Is there a friendship with a woman in your life that your wife isn't part of?
act: If there is one, bring your wife into it or step back from it this week. Tell her you are doing it.

headline: No secret threads. Ever.
prayer: Lord, nothing is hidden from You, so let nothing be hidden from her. Jesus, You took my shame to the cross, and I don't have to hide. Make me a man with no secret conversations.
reading: For nothing is hidden that will not be made manifest, nor is anything secret that will not be known and come to light.
in_jesus: Christ already knows what you would hide, and he went to the cross anyway. In him there is no condemnation, so you can come into the light.
reflect: Is there a text thread you would be uncomfortable handing her right now?
act: From today, if you text a woman, your wife is on the thread. Tell her that rule tonight.

headline: Build guardrails before you need them
prayer: Jesus, I'm not as strong as I think I am. You were tempted and held, and I am not You. Give me the humility to build guardrails before I need them, and the courage to tell a brother about them.
reading: Therefore let anyone who thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall.
in_jesus: Christ stood where you fall. He resisted every temptation, and he intercedes for you at the right hand of the Father.
reflect: Which guardrail are you skipping because you think you don't need it?
act: Ask a younger man at church how he guards his marriage. Share your guardrail and offer to meet with him once a month.

headline: Lead her in prayer, even if awkward
prayer: Father, I want to cover my wife in prayer. Through Jesus, our mediator, help me lead us in praying together, even when it feels awkward. Forgive me for the nights I just rolled over and said nothing.
reading: Likewise, husbands, live with your wives in an understanding way, showing honor to the woman as the weaker vessel, since they are heirs with you of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
in_jesus: Jesus gives you access to the Father. Because of the cross, you and your wife can approach God together, boldly and without fear.
reflect: When did you last pray out loud with your wife?
act: Pray for her by name this morning. Tonight, ask if you can pray with her, and do it out loud.

headline: Serve her daily, not on occasions
prayer: Lord, make serving her a daily habit and not a special occasion. Jesus, You took a towel and washed Your friends' feet. Show me one clear thing I can do for her today, and give me a willing heart.
reading: For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
in_jesus: Christ, the Lord, knelt and washed his disciples' feet, then gave his life. Your freedom in him is a freedom to serve.
reflect: What would she say is the most helpful thing you do for her?
act: Do one act of service for her today tied to something she loves. Do it before she notices it needs doing.

headline: Say the true thing she needs to hear
prayer: Lord, let my words to her be sweet and healing. Holy Spirit, give me something true to tell her today. Jesus, You speak grace and truth to me, so let me speak it to her, and quit holding back.
reading: Gracious words are like a honeycomb, sweetness to the soul and health to the body.
in_jesus: Jesus speaks gracious words that heal. He is full of grace and truth, and his Spirit helps you speak life to the one you love.
reflect: When did you last tell her something specific you love about her?
act: Tell her one specific thing you love about her today. Make it about who she is, not how she looks. Ask the Spirit for the words first.

headline: Nothing washes away this love
prayer: Father, nothing should wash away our love. Jesus, Your love for Your people has never been drowned by their failure. Help me never walk out or walk in without showing her she's loved, and make it a habit.
reading: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man offered for love all the wealth of his house, he would be utterly despised.
in_jesus: The love of Christ cannot be quenched. Not death, not our failures, and not time can separate those he loves from him.
reflect: How do you usually leave the house and come back to it?
act: Kiss her and say "I love you" every time you leave and return, starting this morning.

headline: Love with no agenda
prayer: Lord, love is not self-seeking, and too often mine is. Jesus, You gave and asked for nothing in return. Forgive me for the agenda behind my touch. Let my affection toward her be a gift with no strings.
reading: It does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful.
in_jesus: Christ's love did not insist on its own way. He gave himself without strings, and he teaches you what love looks like when it is not about you.
reflect: Does she ever wonder if your touch is leading somewhere?
act: Give her affection today that isn't aimed at anything. A hug, a hand on her back, a kiss, and nothing more.

headline: What God joined, nothing splits
prayer: Father, You joined us. Jesus, You hold Your people and lose none of them. Don't let anything come between my wife and me, not even good things like work, hobbies, or the kids. Show me what has to move over.
reading: What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate.
in_jesus: Christ holds fast to his bride and will not let her go. What God joined, he sustains, and the same Jesus who holds you can hold your marriage together.
reflect: What good thing has been getting between you and your wife?
act: This week, put one good thing down, a hobby, a project, or a screen. Give that exact time to your wife.

headline: She is the only one
prayer: Lord, let me rejoice in the wife of my youth. Jesus, You are faithful when I am not. Help me give her certainty, every day, that she is the only one for me, and help me tell others why.
reading: Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth.
in_jesus: Christ is faithful to his bride. He keeps every promise, and his faithfulness is the foundation for yours. Your wife can trust a husband who follows him.
reflect: Does your wife have complete certainty that no other woman will catch your eye or your heart?
act: Tell your wife plainly tonight that she is the only one. Then tell a coworker or neighbor what has changed in your marriage this month, and that Christ is why.

headline: Your kids are watching your marriage
prayer: Father, my kids are learning what love looks like by watching me. Through Jesus, let them see me love their mother well, so they know what to look for and who to become. Make me a husband worth copying.
reading: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children will be like olive shoots around your table.
in_jesus: Jesus shows what a covenant looks like. The way you love your wife points your children to how Christ loves his people.
reflect: If your kids marry someone exactly like you, will they be loved well?
act: Show your wife affection in front of your kids on purpose today. Then name one way Christ has changed your marriage this month, and thank him.

headline: Your body was bought. Treat it that way.
prayer: Jesus, this body is Yours. You paid for it with Your blood, and Your Spirit lives in it. Forgive me for treating it like a rental. This month, teach me to honor You with how I move, eat, and rest.
reading: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.
in_jesus: Christ bought you with His own blood, and He sent His Spirit to live in you. Your body is not a project. It is His home.
reflect: If Jesus moved into your body, what kind of house are you keeping for Him?
act: Move your body this morning with purpose. A workout or a walk. Tell Jesus out loud that it is His.

headline: Gym time and prayer time should match.
prayer: Father, through Jesus I come to You. Training has value, but You have more. Keep me from building a strong body around a weak soul. Christ first, then everything else. Show me where I've had that backwards.
reading: For while bodily training is of some value, godliness is of value in every way, as it holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come.
in_jesus: Godliness is not a technique. It is knowing Christ, who gave Himself for you. He is the prize that training only points toward.
reflect: Does your time with Jesus match your time in the gym?
act: Before your workout, pray for the same number of minutes you warm up. Start with the warm-up, then pray.

headline: Your cravings are not your king.
prayer: Jesus, my cravings have been calling the shots. You fasted forty days and did not break. Holy Spirit, I can't white-knuckle this. Help me tell my body no today, and keep me from disqualifying myself or letting down the men watching me.
reading: But I discipline my body and keep it under control, lest after preaching to others I myself should be disqualified.
in_jesus: Jesus answered the tempter with Scripture after forty days without food: man does not live by bread alone. He beat appetite for you, and He gives you His Spirit.
reflect: Who is in charge of you right now: Christ or your cravings?
act: Name one craving to a brother by text before noon. Ask the Spirit for help, then say no to it today.

headline: Run like Christ is at the finish.
prayer: Lord Jesus, I don't want to go through the motions. You ran Your race to the cross and finished it. Give me focus and fight in my training and in my faith today. Don't let me coast. Don't let me coast.
reading: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? So run that you may obtain it.
in_jesus: Jesus is the founder and perfecter of our faith. He endured the cross for the joy set before Him, and He runs ahead of you.
reflect: Are you training to finish strong, or just to show up?
act: Push one set, one mile, or one minute harder than you planned. Offer it to Jesus as you go.

headline: Trophies rust. Christ does not.
prayer: Jesus, men train hard for trophies that rust. You rose with an imperishable body and promised the same to me. Let discipline in the gym spill into my prayer life, my marriage, and my word.
reading: Every athlete exercises self-control in all things. They do it to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable.
in_jesus: Christ rose with a body that cannot decay, and He promises that inheritance to everyone who trusts Him. That is the wreath that lasts.
reflect: What are you really training for, and does Jesus show up in the answer?
act: Write your real "why" for getting healthy on a card. Put Christ and your family in it, then show your wife.

headline: Guilt weighs more than any barbell.
prayer: Jesus, I've carried stress, guilt, and secrets so long my body feels it. You carried my sin in Your own body on the cross. Show me what to turn from, and let Your peace reach my bones.
reading: Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD, and turn away from evil. It will be healing to your flesh and refreshment to your bones.
in_jesus: Christ bore our sins in His body on the tree, and by His wounds we are healed. You do not have to carry what He already carried.
reflect: What are you hauling around that Jesus already carried?
act: Confess one hidden thing to a brother today. Call him before lunch and say it plain.

headline: Every rep can be worship.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You told me to love God with all my strength. Today I'll take that literally. Every rep and mile is for You. Give me the courage to open my mouth about You with someone.
reading: And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.
in_jesus: Jesus said the greatest command is to love God with all your strength, and He kept it perfectly in your place. His strength is counted as yours.
reflect: Is your fitness part of your worship, or just part of your image?
act: Invite a coworker or neighbor who doesn't know Jesus to train or walk with you this week. Tell him who you are really doing it for.

headline: Hard now. Harvest later. Jesus knows.
prayer: Jesus, discipline hurts in the moment. You endured the cross, so You know. Help me push through when it hurts. Remind me the pain today is building a harvest I'll be glad for later, in my body and my character.
reading: For the moment all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
in_jesus: The passage just before this one points us to Jesus, who endured the cross and hostility from sinners so that we would not grow weary or lose heart.
reflect: Which hard choice are you dodging that Jesus would walk straight into?
act: Do the hard thing first today, before email or coffee. Tell Jesus you are doing it for Him.

headline: Food is a gift from Christ's table.
prayer: Lord, thank You for food. Jesus, You gave thanks and fed thousands, and You ate at tables with sinners. Teach me to eat with gratitude, enjoy what You've given, and stop when I've had enough.
reading: So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
in_jesus: Jesus gave thanks over bread, broke it, and fed the crowd. He is the Lord of the table and the Bread of Life. Food is neither His rival nor your enemy.
reflect: Do you treat food as a gift from Jesus, a god, or an enemy?
act: Pray out loud before each meal today. At dinner, eat slowly and ask your family what they are thankful for.

headline: Rebuild the walls. Christ is the foundation.
prayer: Jesus, a man without self-control is a city with no walls, and some of mine are down. Holy Spirit, show me where. Help me rebuild one boundary at a time, leaning on You and not my willpower.
reading: A man without self-control is like a city broken into and left without walls.
in_jesus: When Jesus was mocked and beaten, He did not strike back. He entrusted Himself to the Father. Perfect self-control belongs to Him, and He shares it by His Spirit.
reflect: Where are your walls down: food, drink, screens, or temper?
act: Pick one wall and set a clear boundary in writing. Ask the Holy Spirit to hold you to it and tell one brother.

headline: Sleep is how you trust Jesus.
prayer: Father, I've worn grinding without sleep like a badge. It's really distrust. Jesus slept in a storm because You were in control. Help me go to bed tonight believing You run the world while I rest.
reading: It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives to his beloved sleep.
in_jesus: Jesus slept in the stern while the waves rolled over the boat. Then He stood up and calmed the storm. The one who rules the world also rests in the Father's hands.
reflect: Do you believe Jesus can run your world while you sleep?
act: Phone out of the bedroom tonight. Be in bed by 10 and hand Jesus your list in prayer first.

headline: Jesus told His men to rest.
prayer: Jesus, You told Your men to come away and rest. I need to hear that too. Teach me to rest like You did, without guilt, so I can come back stronger for the people who need me.
reading: And he said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a while.” For many were coming and going, and they had no leisure even to eat.
in_jesus: Jesus called weary disciples away from the crowds and gave them rest. The Lord who never sleeps on His throne also knows what tired men need.
reflect: What would change if you rested because Jesus told you to?
act: Block a real recovery window this week. Stretch, walk, and pray. Tell your wife the time today.

headline: Tired is where Jesus meets you.
prayer: Jesus, I'm tired in body, mind, and spirit. You said to come to You when weary. I'm coming now. Give power to the faint, and fill me up for what today asks of me. I can't do it on empty.
reading: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.
in_jesus: Jesus said, come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. He doesn't scold the weary. He carries them.
reflect: Where are you running on empty, and have you told Jesus?
act: Tell Jesus exactly where you are tired. Then text one brother and ask him to help carry one load.

headline: Wait on Him. Then run.
prayer: Lord Jesus, I keep white-knuckling it alone. Renew my strength as I wait on You. Give me endurance for the long haul, and open my eyes to a worn-out man who needs You. Let me be a friend to him today, not just busy.
reading: But they who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint.
in_jesus: Jesus is the one who actually renews the weary. He invited the tired to come, and He said He would give rest to their souls.
reflect: Are you waiting on Jesus, or just gritting your teeth?
act: Take a walk today with the first five minutes in silent prayer. Then invite a worn-out coworker to coffee and listen to him.

headline: Run to Jesus, not the numbing.
prayer: Jesus, when stress hits I reach for food, a drink, or a screen. Show me what I run to instead of You. Heal what I've been numbing, and be my comfort instead. I'm tired of hiding behind it.
reading: Be not among drunkards or among gluttonous eaters of meat, for the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and slumber will clothe them with rags.
in_jesus: Jesus was tempted in every way and did not sin. He understands your stress, and He invites you to the throne of grace for mercy and help.
reflect: When stress hits, what do you reach for before you reach for Jesus?
act: Next time you reach for comfort, stop and say "Jesus, help me" first. Then decide. Text a brother how it went tonight.

headline: Self-control is fruit, not effort.
prayer: Holy Spirit, I can't white-knuckle my way to self-control. It is Your fruit, not mine. Jesus, You sent Him to me. Stay close and keep me close to You when temptation is loud. Grow Your fruit in me, and let my family see it.
reading: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.
in_jesus: Jesus said it was good for us that He go away, so He could send the Helper. The Spirit of Christ grows self-control in you.
reflect: Are you trying to grow fruit by effort, or by staying close to Jesus?
act: Before each choice about food or drink today, pause and ask the Spirit for self-control. Count how many times you do.

headline: Back on the altar. Again.
prayer: Jesus, You gave Your body for me, so I give mine to You. My hands, my eyes, my appetite, my energy. I keep climbing off the altar. Spirit, help me stay on it today, and when I slide off, pull me back fast.
reading: I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
in_jesus: Christ gave Himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God. Because He did it once for all, you offer yourself in response to His mercy.
reflect: Where have you climbed off the altar, and what pulled you down?
act: Recommit to one health habit you dropped. Pray for the Spirit's help and tell your wife the plan tonight.

headline: Jesus heals bodies and souls.
prayer: Jesus, You healed bodies and forgave sins. I want both healthy. I tend to neglect one while I chase the other. Show me which needs attention today, and help me give it without excuses. Make me whole in both.
reading: Beloved, I pray that all may go well with you and that you may be in good health, as it goes well with your soul.
in_jesus: When Jesus healed a paralyzed man, He first said, your sins are forgiven. He cares for the whole man, body and soul, and He has authority over both.
reflect: Is your body ahead of your soul, or behind it?
act: Give the weaker one an extra 15 minutes today. If it's your soul, read a Gospel chapter. If it's your body, go move.

headline: Joy is medicine Jesus gave you.
prayer: Jesus, I've gotten heavy and serious. You said You spoke so Your joy might be in me. Give me a joyful heart. Let me laugh again, enjoy my family, and stop carrying everything like it all depends on me.
reading: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
in_jesus: Jesus said, I have spoken these things to you that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be full. His joy is not a mood. It is a gift.
reflect: When did you last laugh with your family, and why not today?
act: Do something tonight just for joy with your kids or wife. Play a game and put phones away. Thank Jesus for them.

headline: Give your worries to Jesus tonight.
prayer: Father, I lay my worries down so I can sleep. Every one. Jesus, You are my peace, and You alone keep me safe. Quiet my mind tonight and let me wake up rested, ready to serve my family and my work.
reading: In peace I will both lie down and sleep; for you alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
in_jesus: Jesus calmed the storm with a word, and He says His peace is not as the world gives. You can sleep because He holds you.
reflect: What keeps you up at night, and have you actually handed it to Jesus?
act: Before bed tonight, write down your worries and pray over the list, naming Jesus. Then turn out the light.

headline: Decide before the pressure hits.
prayer: Jesus, give me Daniel's backbone. He decided ahead of time what he wouldn't put in his body. You decided to obey the Father to the cross. Help me decide before the pressure hits, then stick to it.
reading: But Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king’s food, or with the wine that he drank. Therefore he asked the chief of the eunuchs to allow him not to defile himself.
in_jesus: Jesus faced the devil in the wilderness and stood on Scripture. He won where we fall, and He gives that victory to everyone who trusts Him.
reflect: Most bad choices happen because you never decided. What have you not decided yet?
act: Decide today what you won't eat or drink at your next social event. When a coworker asks why, tell him it's about Jesus.

headline: The Lord of the Sabbath says rest.
prayer: Father, You worked six days and rested on the seventh. I work seven and call it success. Jesus, You are Lord of the Sabbath. Teach me the rhythm of work and rest, and give me guts to guard it.
reading: Six days you shall labor, and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work, you, or your son, or your daughter, your male servant, or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates.
in_jesus: Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath. He finished the work of our salvation on the cross, so you can rest in what He did and not what you earn.
reflect: Do you take a real Sabbath, or just a slower workday?
act: Plan one full day of rest this week. This Sunday, invite a man from work or the gym to church with you.

headline: No shortcuts. Jesus took none.
prayer: Lord, keep me honest in how I train and live. No pills, no cheating, no pretending. Jesus, You refused the shortcut in the wilderness. I'd rather grow slowly the right way than fake fast results.
reading: An athlete is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
in_jesus: The devil offered Jesus all the kingdoms without the cross, and Jesus said no. He took the hard honest road to save you.
reflect: Where are you looking for a shortcut that Jesus refused to take?
act: Drop one shortcut today and do it the right way. Tell a brother what it was and ask him to check on you Friday.

headline: Show up. Even when you don't feel it.
prayer: Jesus, I start strong and fade. Holy Spirit, make me faithful. Like the ant, help me just do the work every day, whether I feel like it or not, because You never quit on me.
reading: Go to the ant, O sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise.
in_jesus: Jesus set His face toward Jerusalem and never turned back. His faithfulness to the cross is why yours counts even on your weakest days.
reflect: Are you waiting to feel like it before you do the work?
act: Do your workout or Bible reading today even if you don't feel like it. Ask the Holy Spirit for the first step.

headline: God sees the heart, not the mirror.
prayer: Jesus, You look at the heart, but I keep looking at the mirror. Guard me from vanity. Help me train for Your glory, not my image, and care more about who I am than how I look.
reading: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For the LORD sees not as man sees: man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.”
in_jesus: Isaiah says Christ had no beauty that we should desire Him. He gave up appearance to give you His righteousness, which is what God sees in you.
reflect: Are you training for Jesus' glory or for the mirror?
act: Skip the mirror check once today. Thank Jesus for what your body can do, then do one thing for someone else.

headline: Jesus trains you through the hard fight.
prayer: God, You train my hands for battle. Jesus, You learned obedience through what You suffered. Train my heart too, and prepare me for the fights I can't yet see. Make me steady, humble, and ready when they come.
reading: He trains my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
in_jesus: Jesus, though a Son, learned obedience through what He suffered. He trains you through hard things because He went through them first.
reflect: What fight is Jesus preparing you for right now?
act: Train hard today. Afterward, ask Jesus in prayer what He is teaching you through your hardest thing this week.

headline: The body fades. Christ raises it.
prayer: Jesus, my body is getting older. I feel it in my joints and my recovery. You rose with a glorified body and promised to raise mine. Keep my spirit getting stronger as my body slows.
reading: So we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day.
in_jesus: Christ was raised as the firstfruits, and He will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body. Your decline is not the end.
reflect: Which are you investing in more: the body that fades, or the soul Christ is renewing?
act: Take care of your body today. Then spend twice as long with Jesus in the Gospels.

headline: Even Elijah ate and slept first.
prayer: God, when I'm burned out, meet me like You met Elijah. Not with a lecture, but with food, sleep, and Your presence. Jesus, help me take care of my body, and help a brother who is running on empty.
reading: And the angel of the LORD came again a second time and touched him and said, “Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you.”
in_jesus: Jesus knows tired. He sat worn out at a well and slept in a boat. He is the Bread of Life, and He feeds weary men.
reflect: Who around you is burned out, and what would it cost to help him?
act: Take a meal to a brother who is worn out, or invite him to lunch. Listen, then offer to pray with him.

headline: Guard the heart Christ gave His for.
prayer: Jesus, guard my heart, inside and out. You gave Yours for me. Help me care for the one that beats in my chest and protect the one everything else flows from. Keep both strong, and keep me honest.
reading: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
in_jesus: Christ's heart was pierced on the cross, and blood and water came out. He gave His life so yours could be made new and kept.
reflect: What is poisoning your heart that Jesus already died for?
act: Get your heart rate up today. Then cut off one thing that's been poisoning your heart, and tell your wife what it is.

headline: Jesus wants the whole man.
prayer: God of peace, make me whole. Spirit, soul, and body, kept for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Don't let me ignore any part of what You made. Give me courage to face the part I've avoided.
reading: Now may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
in_jesus: Jesus will return for His people, and He is the one who sanctifies you completely. God is faithful. He will do it.
reflect: Which part of you have you been ignoring: spirit, soul, or body?
act: Book the checkup you have been putting off. Make the call before noon, then tell your wife.

headline: Christ is the strength of my heart.
prayer: Lord Jesus, my flesh will fail someday, no matter how hard I train. When my strength runs out, You are still enough. Holy Spirit, help me keep what I learned this month. Be my portion forever.
reading: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
in_jesus: Christ died and rose, so even when flesh and heart fail, He is your strength and your portion. Your body is His, and He keeps you.
reflect: What did Jesus show you this month about your body and your strength?
act: Look back at this month and write down one health habit you will keep for good. Thank Christ for it, and ask the Spirit to help you keep it.

headline: The cross is where grace starts
prayer: Jesus, You were pierced and crushed for what I did. The punishment I had coming landed on You. This month I want to sit at the cross, not rush past it. Slow me down, and let it change me.
reading: But he was pierced for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the chastisement that brought us peace, and with his wounds we are healed.
in_jesus: Jesus took the punishment that belonged to you, and by his wounds you have peace with God. Grace this month starts with what he did, not with what you will do.
reflect: Which phrase in this passage is hardest to believe was done for you?
act: Read Isaiah 53:5 out loud before you leave the house. Then name one specific sin Jesus was crushed for, and thank him for it.

headline: He loved you at your worst
prayer: Father, You loved me at my worst, not after I cleaned up. I still can't wrap my head around that. Because Christ died for me as a sinner, help me quit performing and come to You as I am.
reading: But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
in_jesus: Christ died for you while you were still a sinner, not after you got your act together. The proof of God's love is a cross, not your track record.
reflect: What are you still trying to clean up before you let God see it?
act: Before noon, tell God plainly the one thing you have been hiding from Him. No polish, no performance.

headline: The Father gave His only Son
prayer: Father, I'm a dad. I can't imagine giving up my son for people who hated me, and You did it for me. Holy Spirit, keep me from ever treating the cross as small. Thank You, Jesus, for going willingly.
reading: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
in_jesus: Jesus is the Son the Father gave, and he came willingly. Everyone who believes in him receives eternal life, not as a reward but as a gift.
reflect: You know this passage by heart. Could you give up your son for people who hate you?
act: Tonight, tell your wife or one of your kids what John 3:16 means to you personally. Ask the Holy Spirit for the words first.

headline: Grace leaves no room to boast
prayer: Lord Jesus, kill my pride. I didn't earn any of this, and every good thing in my life is grace. Strip away the good guy image I hide behind, and make me humble and grateful instead.
reading: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.
in_jesus: Jesus did the work, and salvation comes as a gift received through faith in him. Nothing on your resume is in the transaction, so nothing is left to boast about.
reflect: Where are you quietly proud of being a good guy?
act: Do something generous today for someone who hasn't earned it. Don't mention it to anyone.

headline: Jesus traded records with you
prayer: Jesus, You traded places with me. You took my record and gave me Yours. When guilt and shame come at me today, help me stand on that trade and not on how I feel. Let Your record speak louder than my guilt.
reading: For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
in_jesus: Christ, who never sinned, was made sin for you so that in him you stand righteous before God. That verdict doesn't move with your feelings.
reflect: He took your record and gave you his. Do you actually believe that deal is done?
act: When guilt shows up today, say 2 Corinthians 5:21 out loud, even if you are alone in the car.

headline: Honest prayer, then obedience
prayer: Father, I'll be honest like Jesus was. There are things I don't want to do. Not my will, but Yours. Because Jesus obeyed all the way, give me strength to obey when everything in me wants to run.
reading: Saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
in_jesus: Jesus told the Father the truth about the cost, then went to the cross anyway. He drank the cup of judgment so it would not be yours.
reflect: What is the hard thing in front of you that you keep trying to avoid?
act: Name the hardest thing on your plate this week. Pray Luke 22:42 over it before 9 a.m.

headline: Pressure should drive you to prayer
prayer: Lord, Jesus felt anguish in His body, and He prayed harder. I feel stress in mine and usually react harder. When the pressure hits today, drive me to prayer first, and use me to help someone else carry theirs.
reading: And being in agony he prayed more earnestly; and his sweat became like great drops of blood falling down to the ground.
in_jesus: Jesus carried real agony into prayer so you could carry yours to a Father who hears. He knows pressure from the inside, and he now intercedes for you.
reflect: Where does your stress go: your chest, your sleep, or your temper?
act: Ask a coworker who doesn't know Jesus how he is really holding up today, then listen. Offer to pray for him right there.

headline: Know your weakest hour
prayer: God, my spirit is willing, but my body is weak. Jesus, You prayed while Your friends slept, and You pray for me now. Show me my weakest hours, and help me guard them before I'm already in trouble.
reading: Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
in_jesus: Jesus asked three friends to stay awake with him, and they slept. He went to the cross for them anyway. His grace covers your weak hours too.
reflect: When are you weakest: tired, late at night, or alone?
act: Set one guardrail for tonight. Move your phone out of the bedroom, or text a brother to check on you at 9 p.m.

headline: Forgive the way the cross forgives
prayer: Jesus, You forgave the men driving nails into Your hands. I struggle to forgive a guy who cut me off. Teach me to forgive from the same cross You forgave from, starting with the person I've been avoiding.
reading: And Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” And they cast lots to divide his garments.
in_jesus: Jesus prayed for the men crucifying him while the nails were still going in. The forgiveness you received cost him that much, and it is the forgiveness he asks you to give.
reflect: He forgave while they were still hurting Him. Who are you still holding a grudge against?
act: Pray for the person you have been avoiding, by name, and ask the Father to bless them. Do it before lunch.

headline: Nothing in your hands, welcomed anyway
prayer: Lord Jesus, remember me. I've got nothing to offer You but my need. The thief on the cross had nothing either, and You welcomed him. Holy Spirit, help me see men like us the way You do.
reading: And he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” And he said to him, “Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
in_jesus: Jesus, dying himself, promised paradise to a criminal with no good works and no time left. His grace has never depended on what a man can bring.
reflect: The thief had nothing to offer, and neither do you. Why is that so hard to accept?
act: Think of a man you have written off. Ask the Holy Spirit to soften you, then pray for him by name today.

headline: It is finished. Paid in full.
prayer: Jesus, thank You that it is finished. The debt is paid in full. Help me stop adding to what You completed, stop paying for what's already forgiven, and live today as a man whose debt is gone.
reading: When Jesus had received the sour wine, he said, “It is finished,” and he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
in_jesus: Jesus said it is finished, and he meant it. The debt of sin was paid at the cross, and there is nothing left for you to add.
reflect: Where are you still trying to pay off a debt Jesus already paid?
act: Write down the one past failure you keep paying for. Write FINISHED across it and throw it away.

headline: Forsaken so you never would be
prayer: Father, Jesus was cut off so I never would be. On the days I feel abandoned, remind me You are right here. Make me a man who doesn't walk away from others when they struggle.
reading: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
in_jesus: On the cross Jesus took the abandonment our sin deserved, so those in him are never left. He promised to be with you always, to the end of the age.
reflect: When you feel abandoned, who knows about it?
act: Call or text a man who seems alone right now. Ask him to coffee this week.

headline: He carried your sin on the tree
prayer: Jesus, You carried my sin in Your body on the tree. You took the wounds so I could walk free. Help me die to the sin I keep feeding, and live for what is right.
reading: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed.
in_jesus: Jesus bore your sins in his own body on the cross. By his wounds you are healed, and that healing is why you can say no to what once owned you.
reflect: What sin are you still feeding, knowing what it cost Him?
act: Starve one sin today. When the urge hits, say "Jesus bore this" and walk away from it.

headline: Fix your eyes on Jesus
prayer: Lord, Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before Him. Fix my eyes on Him when today gets hard, in training and in life. Let that joy carry me to run for others, not just for myself.
reading: Looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God.
in_jesus: Jesus is the founder and perfecter of your faith. He endured the cross, scorned its shame, and now sits at the right hand of God. What he began, he finishes.
reflect: What pulls your eyes off Jesus fastest when life gets hard?
act: Invite a coworker or neighbor who doesn't know Jesus to train with you this week. While you work out, tell him what keeps you going.

headline: The tomb is empty
prayer: Risen Lord, I worship You. The tomb is empty, and that changes everything. Let it change something in me this week. Make the resurrection more than a holiday on my calendar. Make it the reason I get up and face this week.
reading: He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.
in_jesus: Jesus is not in the tomb. He rose, as he said he would, and his word has not failed yet. Your sins are paid for, and death is not the end.
reflect: Does the empty tomb change anything about how you live this week?
act: Text one brother "He is risen" today. Tell him one way the resurrection changes your week.

headline: Death lost. Fear lost its grip.
prayer: God, thank You for victory over death through our Lord Jesus Christ. If the grave has lost its sting, fear has lost its grip. Help me walk into today like a man whose fight is already won.
reading: “O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?” The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
in_jesus: Jesus died and rose, and in him the sting of death is gone. The victory is a gift from God through Christ, not something you have to win yourself.
reflect: What fear is running your decisions right now?
act: Do one thing today that fear has kept you from. Make the call, have the talk, or send the email before 5 p.m.

headline: Wages are earned. Gifts are given.
prayer: Lord, I earned death, and You gave me life in Christ Jesus. Thank You for a gift I could never earn. Holy Spirit, make me generous with people who can't pay me back, the way You have been with me.
reading: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
in_jesus: The wages of your sin were death, and Jesus took them on the cross. What you receive in him is eternal life, free and fully paid.
reflect: Are you living like a man on the payroll or a man who was handed a gift?
act: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you someone who can't repay you. Then give that person a meal, a ride, or an hour of your time today.

headline: Mercy saved you, not your resume
prayer: God, You saved me by mercy, not by my resume. My good deeds didn't get me in, and my failures can't kick me out. Because of Jesus, help me rest in that and pass that mercy on today.
reading: He saved us, not because of works done by us in righteousness, but according to his own mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit.
in_jesus: Jesus is the Savior through whom God poured out the Holy Spirit on us. You were washed and renewed by mercy, so there is nothing to earn and nothing to lose.
reflect: Do you act like your good days keep you saved and your bad days threaten it?
act: Show mercy to someone who wronged you today. Skip the lecture, and answer his next message with grace.

headline: Walk up to the throne boldly
prayer: Father, I come to You with confidence because of Jesus, not because of me. Here is what I need today. I am asking boldly, and I am trusting You for mercy and grace right on time.
reading: Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
in_jesus: Jesus is your great high priest. He sympathizes with your weakness, and his finished work is why the throne of God is now a throne of grace.
reflect: Do you come to God with confidence, or do you crawl in ashamed?
act: Before noon, name your biggest need out loud to God. Ask for it plainly, in Jesus' name.

headline: Failure is not your final word
prayer: Jesus, You restored Peter after he denied You three times, then gave him a job. Thank You for not giving up on me after I failed You. Put me back to work, and keep me from hiding behind my failure.
