reading: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he said to him the third time, “Do you love me?” and he said to him, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.”
in_jesus: Jesus went after Peter following the denial, restored him, and gave him sheep to feed. His forgiveness comes with a calling, not a probation period.
reflect: What failure has you convinced Jesus is finished with you?
act: Pick up the work you walked away from after you failed at it. Tell a brother today that you are starting again.

headline: Weakness is where Christ's power shows
prayer: Lord, Your grace is enough for my weakness, even in my body. The injury, the pain, the slowdown with age. Let the power of Christ rest on me right there, and let others see it.
reading: But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
in_jesus: Jesus told Paul that his grace is sufficient and his power is made perfect in weakness. Christ doesn't wait for you to be strong. He shows up in the limp.
reflect: Where are you limited right now, and where is God's grace showing up in it?
act: Tell a coworker or friend who doesn't know Jesus about one weakness you are dealing with, and how Christ has met you in it.

headline: The Father runs to you
prayer: Father, I walked away, and You ran to meet me when I came back. Thank You. Wherever I have drifted, I am turning around today, trusting You to cover the distance I can't. Welcome me home again.
reading: And he arose and came to his father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.
in_jesus: Jesus told this story to show who the Father is. He doesn't wait with a lecture. He runs, embraces, and welcomes sinners home, and Jesus himself receives sinners and eats with them.
reflect: Where have you drifted, and what is one step back?
act: Take one step back toward God today. Open your Bible for ten minutes, or text the brother you have been dodging.

headline: You have peace with God
prayer: God, I am not at war with You anymore. Jesus made peace for me. Help me stop fighting myself too. When I replay my failures tonight, remind me the case is closed, and let me rest in what You have already settled.
reading: Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
in_jesus: Through our Lord Jesus Christ, you have peace with God. He stood in your place, so the argument between you and the Father is over.
reflect: You are not at war with God. Why are you still at war with yourself?
act: Take five minutes of silence today. Sit still and tell Jesus, "I have peace with God because of You."

headline: The Lord laid it on Him
prayer: Lord, I have gone my own way more times than I can count, and You laid it all on Jesus anyway. Holy Spirit, show me where I am still going my own way, and turn me back to Yours.
reading: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—every one—to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
in_jesus: We all wandered like sheep, and the Lord laid the iniquity of us all on Jesus. The Shepherd took the punishment meant for the strays.
reflect: Where are you still going your own way?
act: Turn one area back to God's way today. Decide which one right now, then tell one brother what you chose.

headline: Confess it. He is faithful.
prayer: God, I confess. No excuses, no spin. Here is what I did. Because of Jesus, You are faithful to forgive and cleanse me. Do both today, and give me a brother I can be honest with too.
reading: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
in_jesus: Jesus' blood cleanses us from all sin, and he is our advocate with the Father. When you confess, you are agreeing with the One who already paid.
reflect: What are you hiding that God already knows?
act: Confess one specific sin to God today. Then confess it to one trusted brother, in person or by phone.

headline: God gave His best. Trust Him.
prayer: Father, You did not spare Your own Son. If You gave me Jesus, You will not hold back what I need. I am laying down the worry I keep picking up. You gave Your best, and I trust You with the rest.
reading: He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?
in_jesus: The Father gave Jesus up for us all. If he gave his own Son, nothing you need is too costly for him to give.
reflect: If God gave his Son, why would he hold back what you need now?
act: Write down the one worry you keep carrying and hand it to God in prayer. Then tell a brother you did.

headline: Take up your cross daily
prayer: Jesus, I will take up my cross today. Not once a year. Today. You went first, so show me what dying to myself looks like in the next 24 hours, and give me strength to follow You there.
reading: And he said to all, “If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.”
in_jesus: Jesus went to the cross before he asked you to follow. He denied himself fully for you, and he walks with you into every small death to self.
reflect: Where will saying no to yourself cost you today?
act: Give up one comfort today, like your lunch scroll or the last word in an argument. Spend that time serving someone.

headline: Resurrection power lives in you
prayer: Holy Spirit, You raised Jesus from the dead, and You live in me. Give life to this mortal body. If God cares enough to raise it someday, help me care enough to steward it now and use it to serve.
reading: If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
in_jesus: God raised Christ Jesus from the dead, and the same Spirit now lives in everyone who belongs to him. His resurrection is the guarantee of yours.
reflect: God will raise your body someday. Do you steward it like that matters now?
act: Invite a younger man to train or walk with you this week. Tell him how Jesus has changed the way you treat your body.

headline: Canceled. Not reduced.
prayer: Jesus, You took every charge against me and nailed it to the cross. Canceled, not reduced. Thank You. Help me cancel what others owe me in the same way, whether it's money, an apology, or an old grudge I keep feeding.
reading: And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross.
in_jesus: Christ made you alive together with him, forgave all your trespasses, and nailed the record of debt to the cross. It is canceled, not reduced.
reflect: Do you live like your debt is gone, and do you treat others like theirs is too?
act: Cancel a debt someone owes you today. Tell him it's gone, whether it's money or a grudge.

headline: The King humbled Himself
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are King of kings, and You humbled Yourself all the way to a cross. I struggle to say "I was wrong." Teach me humility, and show me the humble thing to do today.
reading: And being found in human form, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
in_jesus: Jesus, equal with God, became a servant and was obedient to death on a cross. The most humble act in history is also the one that saved you.
reflect: What are you too proud to do that Jesus already did for you?
act: Write down the April passage that hit you hardest, and tell one brother what Jesus did through it. Then apologize to someone or ask for help.

headline: Teach them in the ordinary hours
prayer: Jesus, You taught Your followers on roads, at tables, and by the water. Make me that kind of father. Put Your Word on my heart first, so it comes out at dinner, in the truck, and at bedtime.
reading: And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
in_jesus: Jesus is the Word made flesh, and he walked with his disciples through ordinary days to show them the Father. He does not hand you a program. He gives you himself.
reflect: Faith is caught in a thousand ordinary moments. Which one will you use today?
act: Before bed tonight, ask each of your kids one question about Jesus and listen to the answer.

headline: Lead your kids, don't crush them
prayer: Father, through Jesus I come to You with a short fuse. Show me where I have provoked my kids instead of guiding them. Give me self-control to correct without anger, and the humility to apologize when I get it wrong.
reading: Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
in_jesus: Christ carried your sin, including the harsh words at home, to the cross. Because he forgave you fully, you are free to say "I was wrong" to your kids.
reflect: Do your kids feel led or provoked by you?
act: Apologize to one of your kids today for a specific time you were harsh. Use the words "I was wrong."

headline: Train them by showing them
prayer: Jesus, it is easy to bark corrections and hard to train. Holy Spirit, give me the patience to show, repeat, and model the way my kids should go. I cannot do this on willpower. Make me more like Christ in my own home.
reading: Train up a child in the way he should go; even when he is old he will not depart from it.
in_jesus: Jesus trained twelve men by letting them walk beside him, watch him, and fail in front of him. He did not give up on them, and he has not given up on you.
reflect: Training takes repetition, patience, and example. Which one are you missing?
act: Teach your kid one practical skill today, hands on. Ask the Spirit for patience before you start.

headline: God fathers you with compassion
prayer: Father, You have been patient, tender, and firm with me, and I know You through Jesus. Show me how You father me so I can father my kids the same way. Let them feel Your compassion through me today.
reading: As a father shows compassion to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who fear him.
in_jesus: Jesus said that whoever has seen him has seen the Father. His tenderness toward sinners and the hurting shows exactly how the Father feels about his children.
reflect: Is your fatherhood tender, or only tough?
act: Get down on your kid's level this evening. Ask how they are really doing, then listen without fixing.

headline: Build them up, don't wear them down
prayer: Lord Jesus, don't let me be the reason my kids lose heart. Kill the critical spirit in me that is never satisfied. Help me build them up more than I tear them down.
reading: Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they become discouraged.
in_jesus: Christ did not wait for you to measure up. While you were still a sinner, he died for you. Your kids need that kind of love from their dad.
reflect: Discouraged kids often have dads who are never satisfied. Is that you?
act: Tell your kid you are proud of them, with no conditions and no "but." Do it face to face before tonight.

headline: The Father said it first
prayer: Father, You spoke love over Jesus before he had done any ministry. Thank You that in Christ I am Your beloved son too, not because of my performance. Help me speak that same blessing over my kids.
reading: And behold, a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
in_jesus: At his baptism, before any miracle, the Father declared his love for Jesus. In Christ, that same favor now rests on you by grace, not by your record.
reflect: Do your kids hear love from you before they perform, or only after?
act: Tell each of your kids today, "I love you, and I am proud you are mine."

headline: Arrows are made to be sent
prayer: Lord Jesus, my kids are arrows in my hand, and I want them aimed at You. Keep me strong enough to draw the bow and humble enough to let go when You say. Use my house to reach others.
reading: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior are the children of one’s youth.
in_jesus: Jesus was sent by the Father, and then he sent his disciples the same way. Your family is not the end of the line. It is a launch point for his mission.
reflect: Is your home a place where only your family gets served?
act: Text a coworker or neighbor who does not know Jesus and invite his family over for a meal this week. Send it now.

headline: Your integrity is their inheritance
prayer: God, my choices today land on my kids tomorrow. Let my integrity bless them, not burden them. Make me the same man in private that they see at the dinner table, because Christ is my righteousness, not my image.
reading: The righteous who walks in his integrity—blessed are his children after him!
in_jesus: Jesus lived the righteous life you could not live and gave it to you. You do not build integrity to earn his approval. You walk in it because you already have his righteousness.
reflect: Would your kids be proud to inherit your private life?
act: Make one choice today, where nobody is watching, that you would be glad for your kids to copy. Tell a brother what it was.

headline: Make the call for your house
prayer: Jesus, I am making the call for my family. We will serve You. Help me lead my house by example, not just by announcement, and give me courage when it is not popular.
reading: And if it is evil in your eyes to serve the LORD, choose this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served in the region beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.
in_jesus: Joshua called Israel to choose. Christ chose you first, and he is the Lord worth following. He laid down his life for the house he leads.
reflect: Joshua made the call for his house. Have you made it out loud?
act: At dinner tonight, tell your family that your house will follow Jesus. Then pray over them out loud.

headline: Correction proves you belong
prayer: Father, Your discipline tells me I am Yours. Thank You for caring enough to correct me. Holy Spirit, help me receive it without bitterness and learn what You are teaching me through Christ.
reading: It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?
in_jesus: Jesus took the full judgment your sin deserved, so the Father's correction now is a son's training, not a criminal's sentence. In Christ there is no condemnation.
reflect: How do you respond when God corrects you?
act: Name one hard lesson God is teaching you right now. Tell a brother today and ask the Spirit to help you submit to it.

headline: Correct them like you delight in them
prayer: Lord, You discipline the son You delight in. Too often I discipline out of frustration. Change my heart through Jesus, so my kids know I delight in them even when I am correcting them.
reading: My son, do not despise the LORD’s discipline or be weary of his reproof, for the LORD reproves him whom he loves, as a father the son in whom he delights.
in_jesus: The Father delights in his Son, and in Christ that delight is yours. He corrects you out of love, never rejection. You can correct your kids the same way.
reflect: Do your kids know you delight in them when you correct them?
act: After any correction today, follow it within the hour with a hug and the words "I love you."

headline: Turn your heart toward home
prayer: Jesus, my heart gets pulled toward work, hobbies, and my phone. Turn it back toward my kids. Give me eyes to see them and the strength to be present when I am home.
reading: And he will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a decree of utter destruction.
in_jesus: Christ gave his full attention to people others overlooked, and he came to bring wandering hearts back to the Father. He can turn yours toward home too.
reflect: Where is your heart pointed when you walk in the door?
act: Put your phone in a drawer when you get home tonight. Give each kid ten minutes of undivided attention.

headline: Comfort, urge, and build them up
prayer: Lord Jesus, Paul fathered people by encouraging, comforting, and urging them on. I usually skip straight to urging. Help me do all three today with my kids and the younger men You have put around me.
reading: For you know how, like a father with his children, we exhorted each one of you and encouraged you and charged you to walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.
in_jesus: Jesus is the Good Shepherd who comforts the weary and calls them to follow. He does both, and grace always comes first. Fathers learn the balance from him.
reflect: Encourage, comfort, urge. Which one do you do least?
act: Do your weakest one today. Call or text your kid or a younger man and use it.

headline: Let them copy you following Christ
prayer: Jesus, my kids will copy what I do more than what I say. How I eat, rest, train, and handle stress. Let them copy the good in me, and help me fix the bad before they pick it up.
reading: Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ.
in_jesus: Christ is the one worth imitating. He served, prayed, and obeyed the Father all the way to the cross, and he gives his Spirit so that following him is possible.
reflect: If your kids copied your habits exactly, who would they become?
act: Invite a coworker or younger man who does not know Jesus to train or walk with you this week. Ask him today and tell him why you live the way you do.

headline: Lead on purpose, not by drift
prayer: Father, You chose Abraham to lead his household in Your way, and through Jesus You have called me to do the same. Don't let me drift into passive. Help me lead with conviction and love.
reading: For I have chosen him, that he may command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing righteousness and justice, so that the LORD may bring to Abraham what he has promised him.
in_jesus: The promise God made to Abraham came true in Jesus, the offspring through whom all nations are blessed. You lead your house under the King who kept every promise.
reflect: Are you leading your family on purpose, or drifting?
act: Lead your family in prayer at dinner tonight. If you have skipped it for weeks, say so and start anyway.

headline: Pray for their hearts, not just wins
prayer: Lord Jesus, I pray for my kids' success, but I want their character more. Raise righteous, wise kids in my home. Guard their hearts, and draw each one to You. Teach me to pray for who they are becoming, not only what they achieve.
reading: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; he who fathers a wise son will be glad in him.
in_jesus: Jesus has become wisdom from God for us, our righteousness, holiness, and redemption. Your kids need a perfect Savior far more than a perfect dad.
reflect: Do you pray for your kids' character as much as their success?
act: Pray for each of your kids by name today and ask Jesus to save and shape their hearts. Text your wife what you prayed.

headline: Give them you, not stuff
prayer: Father, You give good gifts to Your children, and the best is Jesus. Holy Spirit, help me give good gifts to mine. Not just stuff, but my time, my attention, and my presence.
reading: Or which one of you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent? If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
in_jesus: God did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all. The Father's best gift is Christ himself, and in him you already have it.
reflect: The best gift is you, present and patient. Are you giving it?
act: Give your kids an hour of your time tonight instead of buying something. Ask the Spirit to help you keep your phone down.

headline: Don't hand them a secondhand faith
prayer: Jesus, I don't want my kids to inherit a secondhand faith. Give me the words to tell them what You have done in my life, and the courage to be honest about where I have been.
reading: We will not hide them from their children, but tell to the coming generation the glorious deeds of the LORD, and his might, and the wonders that he has done.
in_jesus: Christ rescued you from sin and death, and that is a story worth telling. The Gospel gets passed on when people say plainly what Jesus did for them.
reflect: Do your kids know how Jesus changed you?
act: Tonight, tell your kids one true story of how Jesus met you, failures included. Keep it under five minutes.

headline: Speak up when your home needs you
prayer: Lord Jesus, Eli saw it and did nothing. Don't let me be passive in my own home. Give me courage to correct when I need to, and wisdom to do it in love, the way You would.
reading: And I declare to him that I am about to punish his house forever, for the iniquity that he knew, because his sons were blaspheming God, and he did not restrain them.
in_jesus: Jesus spoke truth to people he loved, and he did it with grace, never contempt. He gives you both the courage and the gentleness you need.
reflect: Eli knew and did nothing. What are you too passive to address at home?
act: Name the issue you have been dodging. Talk to the person involved before the weekend, calmly, after praying with your wife.

headline: Earn the right to be heard
prayer: Father, kids listen to dads they respect. Make my life back up my words. Make my instruction worth hearing, because my kids have watched me follow Jesus, even badly. Where I have failed, forgive me and let them see me repent.
reading: Hear, O sons, a father’s instruction, and be attentive, that you may gain insight.
in_jesus: Jesus taught with authority because he lived what he said. He is the Word you can trust, and he forgives the dad whose life has not matched his words yet.
reflect: Does your life back up what you tell your kids?
act: Share one piece of hard-earned wisdom with your kid today. Tell the mistake behind it, and point back to Jesus.

headline: Finish well and bring others along
prayer: Lord Jesus, let me bear fruit into old age. I want to walk my kids through life and hold my grandkids. Help me make choices today that keep me healthy, and let my years count for Your kingdom.
reading: They still bear fruit in old age; they are ever full of sap and green.
in_jesus: Jesus said that those who remain in him bear much fruit. Your health matters, but lasting fruit comes from staying close to Christ.
reflect: What do you want your last decades to be known for?
act: Invite a coworker or neighbor who does not know Jesus to walk or work out with you this week. Ask him today.

headline: Let your kids into your life
prayer: Father, You show the Son everything You do. Show me what You are doing so I can join You. Help me let my kids into my life and work, the way Jesus lived openly with his disciples.
reading: For the Father loves the Son and shows him all that he himself is doing. And greater works than these will he show him, so that you may marvel.
in_jesus: Jesus did only what he saw the Father doing, and he brought his disciples along. He calls you a friend and tells you what the Father is doing.
reflect: Do your kids get to see your life, your work, and your faith?
act: Bring one of your kids along on an errand or task today. Pray out loud with them in the car.

headline: Make your faith worth inheriting
prayer: Jesus, faith passed from Lois to Eunice to Timothy. Let mine pass to my kids too. Make it sincere enough to be worth inheriting, and make You, not me, the one they trust.
reading: I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, dwells in you as well.
in_jesus: Saving faith is not a family heirloom. It is a gift from God through Christ. You can plant and water, but only Jesus brings a child to life.
reflect: What exactly are you passing down to your kids?
act: Write your kids a short letter tonight about why you trust Jesus. Put it somewhere safe.

headline: Don't outsource their faith
prayer: Lord, I cannot outsource my kids' faith to church. Holy Spirit, help me get Scripture into them early and often. Make me the one who points them to Christ, not just the one who drives them there.
reading: And how from childhood you have been acquainted with the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
in_jesus: All Scripture points to Jesus, and he opened it up to his disciples on the Emmaus road. He is the one your kids need to meet on every page.
reflect: Who is teaching your kids Scripture right now? If not you, why not?
act: Read one Bible story about Jesus with your kids tonight. Ask the Spirit to open their eyes, then ask what stood out to them.

headline: Father the boys without fathers
prayer: God, plenty of young men are growing up without a father who shows up. Through Christ, help me father the ones around me. Make my life a model worth following, and give me the time and humility to actually show up for them.
reading: Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled. Show yourself in all respects to be a model of good works, and in your teaching show integrity, dignity.
in_jesus: Jesus called his disciples friends, taught them, and stayed with them when they failed. He is the pattern for any man who mentors a younger one.
reflect: Which young man near you has no one showing up for him?
act: Text a younger man today and set a time this week to buy him coffee or lunch. Ask about his life first.

headline: God is the Father you need
prayer: Father, my earthly dad got some things right and some things wrong. Through Jesus, You are the Father I need. Heal what he could not give me, and help me forgive what he got wrong.
reading: Father of the fatherless and protector of widows is God in his holy habitation.
in_jesus: Jesus forgave the men who nailed him to the cross, and through his death you were adopted into God's family. You can forgive because you have been forgiven.
reflect: Where is your dad's failure still shaping how you father?
act: Name one thing your dad got wrong. Tell God you forgive him, in Jesus' name. If he is living, call him this week.

headline: Let the Potter shape you first
prayer: Lord, I cannot shape my kids well if I won't let You shape me. I am clay in Your hands. Press where You need to press, and make me more like Jesus, the father my family needs.
reading: But now, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
in_jesus: Jesus was broken for you, and the Father raised him up. The Potter does not discard what he reworks. He is shaping you into the likeness of his Son.
reflect: Where are you resisting the Potter's hands as a father?
act: Ask God what he wants to change in you as a father. Write it down and show it to a brother this week.

headline: Fight for your family, then others
prayer: God, Nehemiah told his men to fight for their families. Make me strong to protect mine. Strong in body, steady in mind, and grounded in Jesus, who already won the greater battle. Keep me from fear, and keep me on my feet for my family.
reading: And I looked and arose and said to the nobles and to the officials and to the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes.”
in_jesus: Christ fought the real enemy and won at the cross and the empty tomb. You stand guard over your family in the strength of his finished victory.
reflect: Which strength are you neglecting: physical, mental, or spiritual?
act: Ask a coworker or younger man how his family is doing and offer to pray for him right then. If he does not know Jesus, tell him why you trust him.

headline: Help them grow in every way
prayer: Father, Jesus grew in wisdom and stature and in favor with You and people. Help my kids grow in every way. Show me where each of them needs me most right now, and give me the patience to meet them there.
reading: And Jesus increased in wisdom and in stature and in favor with God and man.
in_jesus: Jesus went through childhood himself, so he knows every stage your kids face. He grew up without sin so he could be the Savior of kids and dads alike.
reflect: Wisdom, body, faith, relationships. Which area is your kid lacking most?
act: Pick the area your kid needs most. Today, ask them one question about it and plan one thing to do together this week.

headline: Be steady, not moody
prayer: Lord Jesus, my discipline swings with my mood. Help me discipline consistently and calmly. Bring peace into my home through clear expectations and steady follow-through, the way You are steady with me. Let my kids feel calm when I walk in, not dread.
reading: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will give delight to your heart.
in_jesus: Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He is steady with you when you are not, and that steadiness is what your home needs from you.
reflect: Do your kids know what to expect from you, or does your mood decide?
act: Set one clear expectation with your kids tonight and follow through calmly. Tell them you are asking Jesus to help you stay steady.

headline: Son first, then father
prayer: Abba, Father. Thank You for making me Your son through Christ. Before I am a dad, I am Your kid. Holy Spirit, help me rest in that today and father my family out of the overflow.
reading: And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!”
in_jesus: By his death and resurrection, Jesus bought you out of slavery and gave you adoption as a son. The Spirit of the Son cries Abba in your heart.
reflect: Do you father from rest in being a son, or from fear of failing?
act: Look back over May. Name one way Jesus changed your fathering and tell your wife or a brother tonight. Then thank him for his grace over the rest.

headline: Your real boss is Jesus Christ
prayer: Jesus, I work for You today. Not for the paycheck, not for the praise, not for the title. Let every job I touch be done like You are watching, because You are. Thank You that Your grace covers where I fall short.
reading: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You are serving the Lord Christ.
in_jesus: Jesus is the Lord Christ you are serving, and he served you first by going to the cross. Your inheritance is not a wage you earned. It is a gift he paid for.
reflect: Would your work look different if you really believed Jesus Christ is the boss you answer to?
act: Before noon, take your least favorite task and do it as worship to Jesus. Do it slowly and well.

headline: Work was God's idea before sin
prayer: Father, You gave Adam work before sin ever showed up. Thank You for mine, even the parts I grumble about. Through Jesus, who worked with his hands, teach me to cultivate and keep what You have put in my care.
reading: The LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.
in_jesus: Jesus was known as the carpenter (Mark 6:3). The Son of God made things with his hands. Honest work is not beneath him, and it is not beneath you.
reflect: Do you treat your work as a curse to survive or a calling from God?
act: Tell your wife tonight which part of your job you complain about most. Then pray together that you would do it as a gift to God.

headline: Provide more than a paycheck
prayer: Lord, I want to provide for my family. Not just money, but presence, protection, and spiritual leadership. Holy Spirit, show me where I have handed over a paycheck and held back the rest. Jesus, lead my house through me.
reading: But if anyone does not provide for his relatives, and especially for members of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
in_jesus: Hanging on the cross, Jesus made sure his mother would be cared for (John 19:26-27). He provided for his own household while carrying the sin of the world. He is the pattern, and he is your strength.
reflect: Where are you providing money but not presence, protection, or spiritual leadership at home?
act: Tonight, give your family one hour with no phones. Read a short passage of Scripture together and pray out loud for each person.

headline: Get excellent, then point to Christ
prayer: Jesus, You did everything well. Make me skillful at my work, not to feed my ego but so people see You through it. Keep me learning, keep me sharp, and keep me humble when I am good at something.
reading: Do you see a man skillful in his work? He will stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
in_jesus: People said of Jesus, "He has done all things well" (Mark 7:37). His skill never served his pride. It served the Father and the people in front of him.
reflect: Are you getting better at your craft, or just getting by?
act: Spend 20 minutes today learning one thing that makes you better at your job. Then ask Jesus who you can serve with it.

headline: Quit dodging the hard task
prayer: Lord, I have gotten lazy in some corners of my work, and You see it. I am not trying to earn Your love by working harder. Jesus already earned it. Give me the drive to finish what I start and do it right.
reading: A slack hand causes poverty, but the hand of the diligent makes rich.
in_jesus: Jesus said, "My Father is working until now, and I am working" (John 5:17). He stayed at the work until he said, "It is finished." Your acceptance rests on his finished work, so you can work hard without fear.
reflect: Where have you gone lazy at work, and will you be honest about it?
act: Pick the task you have been putting off and finish it before lunch. Text a brother when it is done.

headline: Hand Jesus your to-do list
prayer: Father, I hand You my plans today. My calls, my meetings, my jobs, my goals. Through Jesus, commit them to Your purposes and redirect me where I have it wrong. I would rather be corrected than comfortable.
reading: Commit your work to the LORD, and your plans will be established.
in_jesus: Jesus said, "I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me" (John 6:38). He gave his plans to the Father, and the Father is faithful with yours.
reflect: Do you pray over your work, or only over your problems?
act: Before you open email, write your top three tasks and pray over each one by name. Ask Jesus to run the day.

headline: Real rest is found in Jesus
prayer: Jesus, You said to come to You when I am worn out. My mind will not shut off at night, and work is wrecking my sleep. Rescue me from working myself into the ground. Give me rest I cannot produce myself.
reading: What has a man from all the toil and striving of heart with which he toils beneath the sun? For all his days are full of sorrow, and his work is a vexation. Even in the night his heart does not rest. This also is vanity.
in_jesus: Jesus says, "Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matt 11:28). He does not hand you a better schedule. He gives you himself.
reflect: What is your work costing your sleep, your heart, and your family?
act: Today, ask one coworker who looks worn out how he is really doing. Tell him where you find rest, and offer to pray for him.

headline: Work from love, not fear
prayer: God, give me a strong work ethic that comes from love, not fear. Help me outwork my excuses, because Jesus gave himself for me and I am not working to earn anything. Let my effort be thanks.
reading: For even when we were with you, we would give you this command: If anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat.
in_jesus: Jesus said he came "not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many" (Mark 10:45). He worked out of love for you. Now you work out of love for him.
reflect: Where do you coast and call it rest?
act: Write down your biggest excuse. Then do the thing it keeps you from before 10 a.m.

headline: Work your land, skip the scheme
prayer: Lord, keep me on real work, not fantasies. Not the get-rich-quick scheme or the easy way out. Jesus, You are the bread that satisfies. Give me the sense to be faithful with what is right in front of me.
reading: Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread, but he who follows worthless pursuits lacks sense.
in_jesus: Jesus said, "I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger" (John 6:35). Worthless pursuits promise to fill you and never do. He actually does.
reflect: Which scheme or daydream is pulling you away from the work in front of you?
act: Pick the one task that matters most and work on it for 45 minutes with your phone in another room.

headline: Every skill you have is a gift
prayer: Father, every ability I have comes from You. My skills, my energy, my opportunities. Holy Spirit, do not let success make me forget it. Keep me from taking credit that belongs to You and to Jesus.
reading: You shall remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
in_jesus: All things were created through Christ and for him (Col 1:16). Every talent you have came through him. And he gave himself for you, so you never have to prove your worth.
reflect: Success can make a man forget God. Has it done that to you?
act: Name one success you have been taking credit for. Say thanks to Jesus for it out loud, then tell your wife where it really came from.

headline: Seek him before your inbox
prayer: Lord, I reach for my inbox first and for You somewhere after lunch. That is backwards. Jesus, You are the King I say I serve. Help me seek You first and trust You with the rest.
reading: But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
in_jesus: Jesus announced the kingdom and brought it near by his life, death, and resurrection. He is the King you are told to seek first. He came to seek and save the lost (Luke 19:10), and he found you.
reflect: What do you reach for first in the morning: your phone, your inbox, or Jesus?
act: Tonight, set your alarm ten minutes early. Tomorrow, give Jesus those ten minutes before you touch your phone.

headline: Today's bread is enough
prayer: Father, money worries keep dragging me into tomorrow. I am bringing them to You through Jesus. Take my worry, help me do today well, and leave the rest in Your hands. You have never once run out of provision for me.
reading: Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.
in_jesus: Jesus fed thousands with a few loaves (Matt 14:19-21) and taught us to ask for daily bread. He is enough for today, and today is all he asks you to carry.
reflect: What are you anxious about financially, and have you actually told God?
act: Write down your biggest money worry and pray over it with Jesus' words from Matthew 6. Then do today's work and let tomorrow wait.

headline: Honest numbers, honest hands
prayer: Lord, keep me honest in business. No fudged numbers, no padded invoices, no half-truths to close a deal. Jesus, You are the truth. Make me a man whose word at work can be trusted, even when it costs me.
reading: A false balance is an abomination to the LORD, but a just weight is his delight.
in_jesus: Jesus is the truth (John 14:6), and no deceit was found in his mouth (1 Pet 2:22). When you come clean, it does not save you. You are already forgiven in him.
reflect: What number, hour, or claim at work would you change if Jesus read it today?
act: Correct one thing at work today that is not fully honest. Fix it, or tell the person who needs to know.

headline: Start before the crowds do
prayer: Jesus, You got up in the dark to pray before the crowds came. Teach me to begin my day with the Father like You did. Give me the courage to say so to the men around me.
reading: And rising very early in the morning, while it was still dark, he departed and went out to a desolate place, and there he prayed.
in_jesus: Jesus had a full day of need waiting, and he still began with the Father (Mark 1:35). Because of Christ, you now have access to that same Father (Eph 2:18).
reflect: Do your mornings start with the Father or with the noise?
act: Before noon, tell one coworker who does not know Jesus that you pray each morning. Ask what you can pray for him about.

headline: Serve your boss like it's Christ
prayer: God, give me good will toward the people I work for and with. Bosses, clients, customers, even the difficult ones. Jesus took the form of a servant for me. Help me carry that attitude into work today.
reading: Rendering service with a good will as to the Lord and not to man.
in_jesus: Jesus took the form of a servant and became obedient to death on a cross (Phil 2:7-8). Serving a difficult boss is small next to what he did for you.
reflect: Do you serve your boss and customers with good will, or with a bad attitude?
act: Choose the person at work who is hardest to serve. Do something useful for them today without being asked.

headline: Small jobs reveal big character
prayer: Lord, make me faithful in the small stuff. The small jobs, the small details, the small promises. Jesus, You were faithful all the way to death. Where I have cut corners, forgive me and change me.
reading: One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
in_jesus: Jesus was faithful to the Father who appointed him (Heb 3:1-2), all the way to the cross. His faithfulness covers where yours fails, and it is your reason to try again.
reflect: Where are you cutting small corners that no one else would catch?
act: Pick one small job today, one nobody will check, and do it perfectly. Offer it to Jesus.

headline: Your job is a tool. God provides.
prayer: Father, my job is a tool, but You are my provider. Take the panic out of my finances. Holy Spirit, help me trust instead of grip. You did not spare Jesus for me, so I can trust You with this.
reading: And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
in_jesus: God did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all (Rom 8:32). If he gave you Jesus, he will not withhold what you actually need.
reflect: Do you trust the tool or the Source?
act: Tonight, sit down with your wife and pray over your finances together. Name the worry out loud and ask the Spirit for trust.

headline: Give God your first, not leftovers
prayer: Lord, I give You my first and best, not my leftovers. My first hour, my first dollars, my best energy. You gave me Your first and best in Jesus. Let my giving be thanks, not a deal.
reading: Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce; then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will be bursting with wine.
in_jesus: Christ is the firstfruits of those who have died (1 Cor 15:20). The Father gave his first and best, his own Son. Giving in response to that is worship, not a transaction.
reflect: Does God get your first or your leftovers?
act: Open your budget today. If giving is not the first line, move it there and tell your wife why.

headline: Lead like Jesus with the towel
prayer: Jesus, You knelt and washed feet. Make me a servant leader. Let the people under me feel served, not used. Show me who I have been using, forgive me for it, and change how I treat them today.
reading: It shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant.
in_jesus: Jesus, knowing the Father had given all things into his hands, took a towel and washed his disciples' feet (John 13:3-5). Greatness in his kingdom looks like that.
reflect: If you lead people, do they feel served by you or used?
act: Do something today for someone who works for you that they do not expect. Cover a task, bring coffee, or take a hard call.

headline: Know the state of your flock
prayer: God, help me pay attention to what You have put in my care: my finances, my team, my family, my own soul. Jesus, You know Your sheep by name. Make me look closely at what I would rather avoid.
reading: Know well the condition of your flocks, and give attention to your herds.
in_jesus: Jesus says, "I am the good shepherd. I know my own and my own know me" (John 10:14). He knows the true condition of your life, and he laid down his life for you anyway.
reflect: Do you know the real state of your finances, your team, and your family?
act: Open the account, the report, or the conversation you have been avoiding. Look at it today, then pray over it with Jesus.

headline: Come away and rest with Jesus
prayer: Lord, sometimes You have to make me lie down. I confess I will not stop until I am made to. Jesus, my Shepherd, lead me to green pastures and quiet waters. Restore my soul, and let me bring a friend.
reading: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. He leads me in paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
in_jesus: Jesus is the Good Shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). He also told his tired disciples, "Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a while" (Mark 6:31).
reflect: When did you last unplug, and what happened in you when you did?
act: Invite a coworker or neighbor who does not know Jesus on a walk or hike this week, no screens. Tell him what Psalm 23 means to you.

headline: Stop talking. Start moving.
prayer: God, I have talked about some things for far too long. Jesus did more than talk about love. He went to the cross. Give me the courage to take the first real step, and to do it in Your strength.
reading: In all toil there is profit, but mere talk tends only to poverty.
in_jesus: Jesus did not only talk about love. He laid down his life for us (1 John 3:16). His love moved, and it cost him everything, so you can take a step.
reflect: What have you been talking about doing for too long?
act: Take the first real step today. Send the email, make the call, or book the appointment before 5 p.m.

headline: Stay on the wall
prayer: Lord, distractions keep calling me off the wall. Keep me focused on the work You gave me. Jesus, You set Your face toward Jerusalem and did not turn back. Teach me to say no to what pulls me.
reading: And I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?”
in_jesus: Jesus set his face to go to Jerusalem (Luke 9:51), and nothing pulled him off the mission of the cross. He finished it for you, so you can finish what he gave you.
reflect: What is pulling you off the wall right now?
act: Name the one distraction that steals the most from your work. Turn it off or block it until your main task is done.

headline: Pray first, then decide
prayer: God, I make too many decisions in a hurry. Holy Spirit, slow me down and give me wisdom to plan. Jesus, You prayed through the night before a big choice. Teach me to do the same.
reading: The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty.
in_jesus: Before choosing the twelve, Jesus spent the whole night in prayer to God (Luke 6:12-13). The Son did not rush. Because of him, you can ask the Father for wisdom.
reflect: Where are you rushing a big decision at work or with money?
act: Pick one big decision you have been rushing. Pray about it tonight, sleep on it, and ask a brother for counsel before you act.

headline: Your plans sit in his hands
prayer: Lord, my life is a mist, here and gone. All my plans are in Your hands. Jesus, You hold all things together. Help me hold my plans loosely and say "if the Lord wills" and mean it.
reading: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go into such and such a town and spend a year there and trade and make a profit”—yet you do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes. Instead you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.”
in_jesus: Christ holds all things together (Col 1:17). Your life is a mist, but you belong to a risen Lord who holds all of time in his hands.
reflect: Do you plan with Jesus, or just around him?
act: Write "if the Lord wills" at the top of today's plan. Then pray over it with your wife or a brother.

headline: Skip the shortcut. Build slowly.
prayer: God, help me build wealth the right way. Slow, honest, and steady. Keep me from shortcuts that cost me my integrity. Jesus turned down every shortcut for me, so help me turn down mine, even when no one would ever know.
reading: Wealth gained hastily will dwindle, but whoever gathers little by little will increase it.
in_jesus: In the wilderness Satan offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world for one act of worship (Matt 4:8-10). He refused the shortcut and took the long road to the cross for you.
reflect: Where are you tempted to take a shady shortcut?
act: Move something into savings today, even a small amount. Tell your wife so you are building this together.

headline: You have a Boss too
prayer: Lord, people answer to me, and I answer to You. Help me treat them with fairness and respect. Jesus, You are Master over us all. Show me where I have leaned on my position instead of serving.
reading: Masters, treat your bondservants justly and fairly, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.
in_jesus: Christ is the Master of every boss and every worker, and with him there is no partiality (Eph 6:9). He is just, and he bore your sin so you can stand before him.
reflect: If Jesus graded how you lead, what would he say?
act: Before the day ends, recognize one person on your team by name. Be specific about what they did and why it mattered.

headline: Give your days to another man
prayer: Jesus, teach me to number my days. Work will always want more of me. Help me give my health, my family, and my time to the right things, and spend some on a younger man who needs a brother.
reading: So teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom.
in_jesus: Jesus gave his days to twelve men, then gave his life for them. Time poured into another man for Christ's sake is never wasted.
reflect: Is your best time going to work, or to the people God put near you?
act: Text a younger man from work or church and book an hour with him this week. Tell him what you wish someone had told you about Christ.

headline: Rest is trust, not laziness
prayer: Lord, rest is a gift, but laziness is a thief. Give me the honesty to know the difference. Jesus, You slept in a storm because You trusted the Father. Teach me to rest like that and work like I mean it.
reading: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest, and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and want like an armed man.
in_jesus: Jesus slept in the stern during a storm (Mark 4:38), then calmed it with a word. He is Lord over everything that keeps you awake.
reflect: Is your rest a gift you receive, or an excuse you make?
act: Set your alarm tonight and get up on time tomorrow. No snooze. Give the day to Jesus before your feet hit the floor.

headline: Faithful beats famous
prayer: Lord, I do not need to be famous. I need to be faithful. More than any raise or award, I want to hear "well done" from You. Jesus, You were the faithful servant first. Cover my misses and use my wins for Your name.
reading: His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.”
in_jesus: Jesus told this story, and he is the Master who will return. He was the faithful servant first, and he shares his joy with all who trust in him.
reflect: Faithful, not famous. Would Jesus say "well done" about your work this month?
act: Tonight, write down three wins and two misses from June. Thank Jesus for the wins and confess the misses to your wife or a brother.

headline: Courage starts with Christ beside you
prayer: Jesus, You told Your disciples to take heart because You are with them. I want to obey You today, but fear has been steering. Show me where, and go with me into it.
reading: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
in_jesus: Christ is Immanuel, God with us. He promised to be with his people always, to the end of the age, so you never walk into a hard thing alone.
reflect: Where are you disobeying out of fear, and what changes if Christ is already standing there?
act: Before noon, do the one thing you have been afraid to do. Pray first, out loud, in Jesus' name.

headline: He holds you up when you can't
prayer: Jesus, I am not as strong as I act, and You know it. Hold me with Your right hand today. Let me stop pretending in front of You and in front of my brothers.
reading: Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
in_jesus: Jesus carried your sin to the cross and rose again. The hand that upholds you is the same hand that was pierced for you.
reflect: Isaiah gives you five promises. Which one do you need most today?
act: Write that promise on a card and keep it in your pocket. Read it at lunch.

headline: Fear is not from God
prayer: Father, because of Jesus I am Your son, not a slave to fear. Holy Spirit, fill me with power, love, and self-control today, because I cannot manufacture them. Drive out the fear I keep feeding.
reading: For God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control.
in_jesus: Christ has set you free from fear of death and condemnation. In him there is no condemnation, and he sends the Holy Spirit to live in you.
reflect: Where did your biggest fear come from, and why do you keep listening to it?
act: Name your biggest fear out loud, in the car or the shower. Ask the Holy Spirit for help, then pray the reading over it.

headline: Real freedom costs something
prayer: Jesus, You will never leave me or forsake me, and I am counting on it. Thank You for the freedom men paid for, and for the greater freedom You paid for on the cross. Make me brave enough to live free.
reading: Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or be in dread of them, for it is the LORD your God who goes with you. He will not leave you or forsake you.
in_jesus: Christ bought a freedom no army can win. He paid for your sin on the cross, and the Son sets you free indeed.
reflect: What freedom in your life is fear holding hostage?
act: Thank a veteran by name today, in person or by text. At dinner, tell your family what freedom in Christ means to you.

headline: Shrink your fears. Lift up the Lord
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are my light and my stronghold. I have made people and problems bigger than You. Shrink them back down and put You where You belong.
reading: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
in_jesus: Jesus said he is the light of the world, and whoever follows him will not walk in darkness. He took the darkness of the cross so you could live in his light.
reflect: Set your biggest fear next to Jesus. Which one is actually bigger?
act: Call or text the one person you have been avoiding. Set a time to talk this week.

headline: Face the giant in His name
prayer: Jesus, there is a giant in front of me, and I am not going out in my own strength. David came in the Lord's name, and I come in Yours. Give me faith to take the first step.
reading: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.”
in_jesus: David's victory points ahead to a greater one. Christ has already defeated sin and death at the cross and the empty tomb, and he gives that victory to those who trust him.
reflect: What giant is in front of you, and whose name are you bringing to it?
act: Write your giant on paper and pray over it in Jesus' name. Then take one concrete step toward it before dinner.

headline: Trained in secret, sent in public
prayer: Lord Jesus, David fought lions and bears where nobody saw. Prepare me in the hidden places too. Use my early mornings with You to ready me for a battle I cannot see yet.
reading: But David said to Saul, “Your servant used to keep sheep for his father. And when there came a lion, or a bear, and took a lamb from the flock, I went after him and struck him and delivered it out of his mouth. And if he arose against me, I caught him by his beard and struck him and killed him.”
in_jesus: Jesus rose early to pray alone before the crowds found him, and he obeyed the Father all the way to the cross. His hidden faithfulness carried a public rescue.
reflect: What are you doing in private that prepares you for what God may ask of you in public?
act: Invite a coworker who does not know Jesus to walk or train with you this week. Ask him one real question about how he is doing.

headline: Speak up. You are here for this
prayer: Jesus, You spoke the truth when it cost You everything. Maybe I am here for such a time as this. Do not let me hide in silence when someone needs a voice.
reading: For if you keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will rise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
in_jesus: Christ told the truth before Pilate and went to the cross for people who stayed silent, including his own friends. He forgives cowardly silence and sends his people to speak.
reflect: Where are you staying silent when you should speak?
act: Say the hard thing that needs saying to one person today. Do it with love, and do it before the day ends.

headline: Even if He doesn't, I will
prayer: Jesus, You are able to deliver me. But even if You do not, I will not bow. Make my obedience unconditional, not a deal I am trying to strike with You.
reading: If this be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image that you have set up.
in_jesus: In Gethsemane Christ prayed, not my will, but yours, and obeyed all the way to death. His obedience, not yours, is what makes you right with God.
reflect: Is your obedience conditional on God giving you the outcome you want?
act: Pick the one area where you have been bargaining with God. Obey him there today and leave the outcome with him.

headline: Bold men have nothing to hide
prayer: Father, guilty men run when no one is chasing them, and I have run. Because Jesus took my guilt, I can stand. Holy Spirit, make me bold today, because I cannot do it alone.
reading: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion.
in_jesus: Christ bore your guilt on the cross, so the boldness in Proverbs is a gift, not a performance. His blood cleanses a conscience that has been running.
reflect: What have you been running from that Christ has already paid for?
act: Confess what you are hiding to one trusted brother or to your wife today. Then receive the forgiveness Jesus already bought.

headline: They had been with Jesus
prayer: Jesus, Peter and John were ordinary men, but people could tell they had been with You. Let them see that in me. Let my courage come from time with You, not from my resume.
reading: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were uneducated, common men, they were astonished. And they recognized that they had been with Jesus.
in_jesus: Jesus called ordinary fishermen, restored Peter after he denied him, and filled them with his Spirit. Their boldness came from him, not from them.
reflect: Could anyone say you have been with Jesus? How much time are you giving him?
act: Give Jesus ten minutes before lunch, phone away, in Scripture and prayer. Then go face your day.

headline: When fear comes, trust. Right then
prayer: Jesus, fear will show up today. Make trusting You my first move, not my last resort. Not after I figure it out. Right then, in the moment.
reading: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
in_jesus: Jesus slept in the boat during the storm and stilled it with a word. The one who rules the wind is the one with you when fear hits.
reflect: David said when, not if. What do you usually do first with your fear?
act: Memorize Psalm 56:3 today. Say it out loud the next time your stomach drops, and tell your wife or a brother you are learning it.

headline: Get out of the boat
prayer: Jesus, call me out of the boat. I would rather sink reaching for You than sit safe and never move. When I look at the waves, take hold of my hand.
reading: He said, “Come.” So Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water and came to Jesus. But when he saw the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, “Lord, save me.” Jesus immediately reached out his hand and took hold of him, saying to him, “O you of little faith, why did you doubt?”
in_jesus: Jesus reached out and caught Peter the moment he began to sink. He does not wait for your faith to be strong. He takes hold of you when it fails.
reflect: What boat are you hiding in, and what is Jesus calling you to step into?
act: Take one faith risk before noon: a conversation, a call, a decision. Keep your eyes on Jesus, not the waves.

headline: Strong for the long haul
prayer: Lord Jesus, Caleb was ready to take a mountain at 85. Keep me strong in body and in faith for the long haul. Give me courage to start the hard thing that builds it.
reading: I am still as strong today as I was in the day that Moses sent me; my strength now is as my strength was then, for war and for going and coming.
in_jesus: Caleb's strength came from the Lord who went with him. Christ is that Lord, and he invites the weary to come to him and find rest.
reflect: What will your body and your faith be ready for at 85 if you keep living like this?
act: Invite a younger man to walk or train with you this week. Ask him where he needs to grow in faith, and disciple him as you go.

headline: Run to Him first
prayer: Father, things are shaking around me. Because of Jesus I can come to You as my refuge. Help me run to You first today, not last.
reading: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear though the earth gives way, though the mountains be moved into the heart of the sea.
in_jesus: Because of Christ's death for you, the way to the Father is open. You can come with confidence and find mercy and grace in your time of need.
reflect: What is shaking right now, and is God your first call or your last?
act: The first time trouble hits today, stop and pray for thirty seconds before you do anything else.

headline: He has already overcome the world
prayer: Jesus, You never promised me an easy life. You promised trouble, and You promised You have overcome it. I take heart in that today, and I will pass it on.
reading: I have said these things to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world.
in_jesus: Jesus said this the night before his arrest. He then went to the cross and rose again, so his victory over the world is a finished fact, not a hope.
reflect: Are you more focused on the trouble Jesus promised or the victory he won?
act: Text a man in a hard season today. Tell him you are praying for him and send him this passage.

headline: Finish the course Christ gave you
prayer: Lord Jesus, Paul counted his comfort as nothing next to finishing what You gave him. Show me my course. Holy Spirit, keep me moving toward it when I want to coast.
reading: But I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God.
in_jesus: Jesus set his face toward Jerusalem and finished the work the Father gave him. On the cross he said, "It is finished," so you run your race in his strength.
reflect: What course has Jesus given you, and what comfort are you protecting instead?
act: Write down the one thing God has called you to in your home, work, or church. Take the next small step toward it today.

headline: God calls you mighty. Believe Him
prayer: Father, Gideon was hiding when You called him a mighty man. Through Jesus You see who I will become, not just who I am. Call me forward and give me courage to step in.
reading: And the angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
in_jesus: Christ clothes weak men in his own righteousness. God sees you in his Son, and the promise he gave Gideon is yours: the Lord is with you.
reflect: Where are you hiding when God has already said he is with you?
act: Say yes today to one thing in your church or family that you have dodged because you feel unqualified. Tell a brother you said yes.

headline: Fear God. Stop fearing men
prayer: Jesus, I care too much about what people think. Help me honor the Father more than their approval. Free me from needing it, since Your approval is already mine.
reading: And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
in_jesus: Christ secured God's approval for you by his cross. You do not have to earn the applause of men when the Father is already pleased with those in his Son.
reflect: Whose opinion controls you: your boss, your buddies, your wife? What changes if God's comes first?
act: Make one decision today based only on what Scripture says, even if someone will be unhappy with it.

headline: Courage is showing up scared
prayer: Jesus, courage is not a feeling. It is showing up and doing the work. Help me do the work today, scared or not, because You will not leave me until it is finished.
reading: Then David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous and do it. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not leave you or forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.”
in_jesus: Christ finished the work the Father gave him, and he promised to be with his people always. You do the work in front of you with him beside you.
reflect: What work are you putting off until you feel brave enough?
act: Pick the task you have been avoiding and work on it for thirty minutes before lunch. Pray in Jesus' name first.

headline: Face the news. His grip is firm
prayer: Lord Jesus, steady my heart for whatever news comes. I have avoided some things because I fear the answer, including my health. Make me a man who faces bad news with trust, not avoidance.
reading: He is not afraid of bad news; his heart is firm, trusting in the LORD.
in_jesus: Christ holds the keys of death and Hades, and he said, "Do not be afraid, I am the first and the last." No diagnosis has the final word over you.
reflect: What are you avoiding because you are afraid of the answer?
act: Book the checkup you have been dodging. Then ask a coworker when he last went, and offer to pray for him if he is carrying something.

headline: Your strength runs out. His doesn't
prayer: Jesus, my strength is gone by mid-afternoon. Yours never is. Remind me before every hard moment today that I am strong in You, not in me.
reading: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might.
in_jesus: Christ told Paul that his power is made perfect in weakness. The Jesus who rose from the dead is the strength you lean on when yours is spent.
reflect: Where are you running on your own power, and where is it already failing?
act: Set three phone alarms today. When each one goes off, stop for ten seconds and ask Jesus for strength.

headline: God is for you. Stand
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are on my side. What can man really do to me? Help me stand on my convictions today, even if I stand alone.
reading: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear. What can man do to me?
in_jesus: Jesus stood before Pilate with his friends scattered, then rose from the dead. He knows what standing alone costs, and he stands with you.
reflect: What is the worst people can actually do to you, compared to who is on your side?
act: Hold your ground on one conviction today at work or with friends, even if it is unpopular. Stay kind while you do it.

headline: Honor Christ with your body
prayer: Father, let Christ be honored in my body, in how I work, train, serve, and treat people. Holy Spirit, give me the boldness, because I cannot produce it. Let Jesus get the credit, not me.
reading: As it is my eager expectation and hope that I will not be at all ashamed, but that with full courage now as always Christ will be honored in my body, whether by life or by death.
in_jesus: Jesus gave his body on the cross for you and rose in a body. Yours is now a temple of his Holy Spirit, bought with a price.
reflect: How are you using your body to honor Christ?
act: Use your body today to serve someone: carry something, fix something, or train with a purpose. Do it as for Jesus.

headline: This battle belongs to God
prayer: Lord Jesus, I have been fighting this one alone, and I am losing. This battle is Yours, not mine. I will do my part, and I hand You the outcome.
reading: And he said, “Listen, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat: Thus says the LORD to you, ‘Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed at this great horde, for the battle is not yours but God’s.’”
in_jesus: Christ fought the decisive battle at the cross and won. He disarmed the powers and triumphed over them, so you fight from his victory, not for it.
reflect: What battle are you fighting alone that already belongs to Christ?
act: Name that battle to one brother today and ask him to pray with you right then. Do your part, and leave the result with God.

headline: See the promise, not the giants
prayer: Father, ten men saw giants. Caleb saw Your promise. Give me Caleb's faith through Jesus, and let me speak faith where everyone around me is speaking fear.
reading: But Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “Let us go up at once and occupy it, for we are well able to overcome it.”
in_jesus: Every promise of God is Yes in Christ. Jesus is the proof that God keeps his word, and his resurrection shows nothing can stand against it.
reflect: Ten men saw giants. Caleb saw God's promise. What do you see?
act: In your next tense conversation, say one sentence of faith out loud, like "God is with us in this." Do it before dinner.

headline: Be ready to tell your story
prayer: Jesus, I talk about everything except You. Give me courage to share my faith with gentleness and respect. Make me ready when someone asks about the hope in me.
reading: But in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect.
in_jesus: Christ is the hope you are asked about. He died for sinners and rose again, and he promised to be with you as you go and tell.
reflect: Could you explain what Jesus has done for you in two minutes?
act: Write your two-minute story: life before Christ, how you met him, life now. Text it to one brother and practice it out loud.

headline: Strengthen a brother who is shaking
prayer: Lord Jesus, some of my brothers have weak knees and anxious hearts, and they will not say it. Use me to strengthen them. Give me the words and the invitation that gets them moving.
reading: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Say to those who have an anxious heart, “Be strong; fear not! Behold, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God. He will come and save you.”
in_jesus: Jesus is the God Isaiah promised, come to save. He healed the weak and welcomed the anxious, and he still does it through his people.
reflect: Which brother is struggling and too proud to say it?
act: Invite a man at work or church who seems weighed down to walk or work out with you this week. Ask how he is really doing.

headline: God is for you. Move
prayer: Father, because Jesus died for me, You are for me. If that is true, nobody can stand against me. Help me stop hesitating and do the thing I have been putting off.
reading: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
in_jesus: God did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all. If he gave Christ for you, he will not hold back what you need to obey him.
reflect: If God gave his Son for you, what are you still waiting for?
act: Make the call, send the email, or have the talk you have been dreading. Do it before noon.

headline: Courage grows from hope in Christ
prayer: Lord Jesus, my courage grows from my hope, and my hope is in You. Strengthen my heart today. Remind me what I am trusting You for, and keep me holding on.
reading: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the LORD!
in_jesus: Christ is our living hope. He rose from the dead, so what you are waiting for is certain, not wishful.
reflect: What are you hoping in when fear shows up?
act: Write down three things you are trusting God for. Read them to your wife or a brother tonight and pray over them together.

headline: Finish strong. Stay faithful to the end
prayer: Jesus, courage is not one big moment. It is a lifetime of small ones. Holy Spirit, keep me faithful to the end and from quitting halfway, because I cannot finish on my own.
reading: Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and for ten days you will have tribulation. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.
in_jesus: Jesus is the one who died and came to life. He gives the crown of life to those who stay faithful, and he holds you while you do.
reflect: Looking back at July, where did Christ make you braver than you were on the first?
act: Tonight, review July. Write down one place Christ carried you through fear, tell a brother, and ask him to hold you to finishing strong.

headline: Brotherhood is Christ's idea, not ours.
prayer: Jesus, I don't need more buddies who nod along. This month, give me brothers who sharpen me, sparks and all. Make me a man who sharpens them in Your name.
reading: Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another.
in_jesus: Jesus calls his people into one family, and he uses brothers to shape us. He finished the work of our salvation, so we can take correction without fear.
reflect: Who in your life is allowed to push back on you, and when did you last listen?
act: Text one friend today: "Where do you see me drifting?" Then listen without defending yourself.

headline: Many buddies, few brothers.
prayer: Father, through Jesus, the friend who sticks closer than any brother, I admit I know a lot of guys and have few real friends. Show me one man to invest in, and help me start.
reading: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
in_jesus: Jesus calls his people friends (John 15:15), and Hebrews 2:11 says he is not ashamed to call us brothers. He came after us first.
reflect: Who is the one man who would drop everything for you, and would you do the same for him?
act: Call that one friend before noon. Not a text. A call.

headline: Carry him. That is the law of Christ.
prayer: Jesus, You carried my sin to the cross. Holy Spirit, help me carry my brother's load, not just feel bad for him. Don't let me stay on the sidelines. Get me to his door.
reading: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
in_jesus: Christ bore our sins in his body on the tree (1 Peter 2:24). When we carry a brother's burden, we follow the one who carried ours.
reflect: Who around you is under a heavy load right now, and what have you actually done about it?
act: Before dinner, call or visit one man who is hurting. Ask what he needs, or bring him a meal.

headline: Show up. Christ's body needs you.
prayer: Jesus, You are the head of the church, and I keep treating it like an option. Keep me showing up for my brothers. Make me the man who spurs others on, not the one they have to chase down.
reading: And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
in_jesus: Jesus gave himself up for the church (Ephesians 5:25). Meeting with his people is not a duty we earn. It is joining the body he bought with his blood.
reflect: When did you last skip your group, and what was the real reason?
act: Put your next group meeting on your calendar right now. No group? Ask your pastor today to help you find one.

headline: Confess to a brother and be healed.
prayer: Father, I tell You my sins and hide them from everyone else. Because Jesus already took my guilt, give me the guts to be honest with another man. I want to be healed.
reading: Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person has great power as it is working.
in_jesus: Jesus bore the sins we hide, so nothing you confess can shock him. He sympathizes with our weakness (Hebrews 4:15), and he gives us brothers to speak it to.
reflect: Who knows your real struggle, not the cleaned-up version?
act: Tell one trusted brother the struggle you have been hiding. Do it face to face or by phone by Friday.

headline: Want your brother to win.
prayer: Jesus, You gave up everything so I could win. Kill the competition in me. Help me cheer for my brothers the way Jonathan cheered for David, even when it costs me.
reading: As soon as he had finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
in_jesus: Jonathan gave up a throne for David, and Jesus gave up far more. Though rich, he became poor for us (2 Corinthians 8:9), so we could share his inheritance.
reflect: Is there a brother whose success stings you, and why?
act: Today, do one thing that helps a friend get ahead, even if it costs you time or credit.

headline: Hold arms up. Then reach out.
prayer: Lord Jesus, even Moses needed men to hold his arms up, and I'm no stronger. Give me brothers who hold me up in my faith and my health. Show me a man who needs me too.
reading: But Moses’ hands grew weary, so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it, while Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side. So his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
