in_jesus: Heaven sings to the Lamb who was slain (Rev 5:12). Christ is worthy of loud praise, and He doesn't grade your pitch.
reflect: When did you last worship out loud?
act: Put on a worship song about the cross and sing it out loud in the car. Let your kids hear you.

headline: He never sleeps, so you can rest
prayer: Jesus, You keep watch so I can rest. The holidays knocked my routine sideways. Help me get back on track with sleep and training, trusting You to hold what I can't. Teach me that rest is trust, not laziness.
reading: He will not let your foot be moved; he who keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
in_jesus: Jesus slept in the storm and then stilled it (Mark 4:38-39). The same Christ keeps watch over you, and none He holds will be snatched away (John 10:28).
reflect: What are you carrying that Christ is already watching over?
act: Ask a coworker who seems worn down how he's holding up. Offer to pray for him in Jesus' name, right there.

headline: Jesus is the gift you can't lose
prayer: Father, of all the gifts on my list, Jesus is the one I can never lose. Thank You for Him. Put Christ at the top of my gratitude, where He belongs. Let every other blessing point me back to Him.
reading: Thanks be to God for his inexpressible gift!
in_jesus: God gave Christ Jesus to die for sinners and raised Him on the third day. Every other thing you thank God for rests on that gift.
reflect: Is Jesus at the top of your gratitude list?
act: Put Jesus first on today's gratitude list. Then write what He gave you at the cross, and thank Him for each.

headline: He is your portion. That's enough.
prayer: Jesus, You are my portion. If I have You, I have enough. Let this month of gratitude settle deep, and keep me hoping in You when the list runs short. You've been enough all month, and You will be tomorrow.
reading: “The LORD is my portion,” says my soul, “therefore I will hope in him.”
in_jesus: Christ gave Himself for us, and in Him every promise of God is yes (2 Cor 1:20). The man who has Jesus already has enough.
reflect: If Christ is your portion, what are you still reaching for?
act: Read your gratitude list from this month tonight. Circle where Jesus showed up, thank Him, and tell one brother.

headline: The King has come
prayer: Jesus, You are Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. December gets loud and I get busy. Rule my month, and pull my eyes off the to-do list and onto You, my King.
reading: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder, and his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
in_jesus: Jesus is the child born and the Son given, and the government rests on his shoulder. He did not wait for us to get it together. The King has come to us.
reflect: Four names for one King. Which one do you need Jesus to be for you right now?
act: Pick that name, then pray to Jesus by it at breakfast, at lunch, and before bed today.

headline: Life comes out of the stump
prayer: Father, Israel looked like a dead stump, and through Jesus You grew a King out of it. You bring life out of what looks finished. Because of Him, I'm asking You to do that in my dead places.
reading: There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit.
in_jesus: Jesus is the shoot from the stump of Jesse. He came from a family line that looked finished, and he walked out of a tomb that looked final. Christ brings life out of death.
reflect: Israel looked finished, and God grew a King. What in your life looks dead?
act: Text one brother before noon. Name that dead area and ask him to pray for it with you.

headline: The King came from a nothing town
prayer: Lord Jesus, You were born in a town too small to matter, and You are the King. You use small places and small men. Holy Spirit, help me do the small thing in front of me today in Your strength, not mine.
reading: But you, O Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are too little to be among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose coming forth is from of old, from ancient days.
in_jesus: Christ, the ruler from ancient days, chose Bethlehem and a feeding trough over a palace. He does not need us to be big. He came low to save us.
reflect: Bethlehem was too little to count. Where are you telling yourself you're too small for God to use?
act: Finish the small task you keep putting off, like the call, the report, or the dishes. Ask the Spirit for help before you start.

headline: Joseph covered her instead of exposing her
prayer: Father, Joseph believed he'd been wronged, and he still chose to protect Mary. Give me Joseph's character. Through Jesus, who covers my sin instead of exposing it, make me a man who protects instead of getting even.
reading: And her husband Joseph, being a just man and unwilling to put her to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly. But as he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.”
in_jesus: Jesus entered the world under the care of a man who chose mercy over payback. On the cross, Christ took our shame so that God covers us instead of exposing us.
reflect: When you feel wronged, do you protect people or expose them?
act: Today, when someone who wronged you comes up in conversation, say something good about him or say nothing.

headline: Joseph woke up and obeyed
prayer: Lord Jesus, Joseph woke up and did what the angel said. No delay, no debate. Show me what I've been sitting on. Because You obeyed the Father all the way, give me the guts to move today.
reading: When Joseph woke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him: he took his wife.
in_jesus: Jesus obeyed the Father perfectly, all the way to the cross, so our obedience never has to earn anything. Christ's yes makes our yes possible.
reflect: What has God already told you to do that you keep putting off?
act: Do it before noon today. If it takes a conversation, start it with a call or text.

headline: His name means the Lord saves
prayer: Jesus, Your name means the Lord saves. You came to save me from my sins, not just my circumstances. I'm bringing You the sin I keep going back to. Save me from it, and keep me from hiding it.
reading: She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
in_jesus: Jesus came to save his people from their sins, and he did it on the cross. Christ does not just fix our circumstances. He deals with the thing we keep going back to.
reflect: What sin are you still carrying that you need Jesus to save you from?
act: Name that sin out loud to Jesus this morning. Then text one brother and tell him, so you are not fighting it alone.

headline: Don't drift through December
prayer: Lord Jesus, the holidays are when I drift. Parties, travel, late nights, too much food. You went to the cross on purpose, so keep me on purpose. Help me make a simple plan for my body and soul, and stick to it.
reading: So I do not run aimlessly; I do not box as one beating the air.
in_jesus: Jesus set his face toward Jerusalem and never drifted. Christ finished what the Father gave him to do, so we run our race from his grace, not to earn it.
reflect: Where do you drift every December, and who would notice if you did?
act: Invite a coworker or neighbor who doesn't know Jesus to a workout or coffee this week. Tell him why you're keeping a plan this month.

headline: Nothing is impossible with God
prayer: Father, nothing is impossible for You, and You proved it by sending Your Son through a virgin's womb. I've written some things off as hopeless. Because of Jesus, stir up my faith to ask again.
reading: For nothing will be impossible with God.
in_jesus: Jesus entered the world through a miracle, and he walked out of a sealed tomb. Christ is proof that no situation is too far gone for God.
reflect: What have you written off as hopeless, and have you actually asked God about it?
act: Write that impossible thing on a card. Pray over it out loud tonight with your wife or a brother, and keep the card where you'll see it.

headline: The King had no room
prayer: Jesus, You were born in a feeding trough because there was no room. Don't let there be no room for You in my month. You came humble. Make me humble, and make room in my calendar for You.
reading: And she gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in swaddling cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
in_jesus: Christ left the throne of heaven for a feeding trough. He made himself low so that he could make room for us in the Father's house.
reflect: If your calendar shows what you love, is there any room in it for Jesus?
act: Block 30 minutes this week for Scripture and prayer. Set the day and time before you close this app.

headline: Good news for working men
prayer: Father, You announced the greatest news in history to shepherds on the night shift. Through Jesus, the Savior and Lord, I thank You that it's for guys like me. Holy Spirit, give me boldness to share it with somebody this week.
reading: And the angel said to them, “Fear not, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.”
in_jesus: Jesus is the Savior, Christ the Lord, born in the city of David. The news came to men working the night shift because he came for all people, not just the polished ones.
reflect: The shepherds heard first. Who at your work needs to hear it from you?
act: Ask one coworker how his Christmas is going, then tell him one thing Jesus means to you. Ask the Spirit for the opening first.

headline: Glory to God before the to-do list
prayer: Glory to You, God, in the highest. Before the shopping, the schedule, and the stress, You get my praise. Let me start with You, not the noise. Through Jesus, my peace, settle Your peace on my house today.
reading: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those with whom he is pleased!
in_jesus: Jesus is the peace the angels sang about. Christ reconciled us to God by his blood, so peace is something he gives, not something we manufacture.
reflect: Does your Christmas start with God's glory or with your to-do list?
act: Before you pick up your phone this morning, spend five minutes praising Jesus out loud. Read Luke 2:14 first.

headline: Slow down and treasure it
prayer: Lord Jesus, Mary treasured these things and thought on them. I rush past everything. Slow me down to remember what You've done this year, and let it sink in deep enough to change me, not just pass through me.
reading: But Mary treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart.
in_jesus: Jesus was the thing Mary pondered, the Son of God lying in her arms. Christ is worth more than a quick glance. He invites us to sit and take him in.
reflect: In the rush of December, what has God been doing that you haven't noticed?
act: Take ten quiet minutes tonight with your phone off. Write down three things Jesus did in your life this year.

headline: Back to the same fields, changed
prayer: God, the shepherds went back to the same fields, but they went back praising You. Because I've met Jesus, make me a man who goes back to work changed. Let my crew see the difference.
reading: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, as it had been told them.
in_jesus: Jesus did not pull the shepherds out of their jobs. He met them there and sent them back praising. Christ changes the man first, then the work.
reflect: Has meeting Jesus changed how you show up at work?
act: Thank one coworker by name today for something specific he does. Work the rest of the day as if Jesus is your boss.

headline: Hold the line this season
prayer: Lord, there's a season for everything, and this one is about holding the line. Jesus, You stayed faithful when it cost You everything. Don't let me quit on my health or my time with You just because I'm busy.
reading: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven.
in_jesus: Jesus came at the right time and finished what he started. Christ held the line all the way to the cross, so our small faithfulness rests on his finished work.
reflect: What good habit are you about to drop because December is busy?
act: Invite a guy who doesn't know Jesus to a 20-minute workout or walk today. Keep it simple and ask how his December is going.

headline: God moved into the neighborhood
prayer: Jesus, You are the Word made flesh. You know hunger, exhaustion, and pain in a body like mine. Thank You for coming that close. Help me be that present for someone else this week, with my time and my full attention.
reading: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
in_jesus: Jesus took on flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. Christ did not save us from a distance. He came close enough to touch.
reflect: Who in your life needs you in the room, not just a text?
act: Show up in person today for someone who is hurting. Walk into his office or knock on his door instead of texting.

headline: The King became a servant
prayer: Lord Jesus, You had every right to hold on to Your status, and You emptied Yourself instead. Teach me to serve. Show me what status I'm clinging to, and help me let it go, because You already gave up more for me.
reading: Who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, by taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men.
in_jesus: Jesus, who is God, emptied himself and took the form of a servant. Christ stooped to the lowest place for us, so no job is beneath his followers.
reflect: What status or pride are you holding on to that keeps you from serving?
act: Do a humble job at home today that you usually leave to someone else, like the trash or the dishes. Don't mention it.

headline: Wise men brought their best
prayer: Jesus, wise men traveled a long way and bowed with their best. I want to bring You mine. Holy Spirit, help me hand over the habit I've been holding back, along with my time and my money.
reading: When they saw the star, they rejoiced exceedingly with great joy. And going into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Then, opening their treasures, they offered him gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.
in_jesus: Jesus received worship as a child and deserved it. Later he gave what no gift could match: his own life as a ransom for many. Christ is worth our best.
reflect: The wise men gave Jesus their treasure. What are you still holding back?
act: Pick one: a set amount of money, an hour of your time, or a habit. Give it to Jesus today, and ask the Spirit to carry you through.

headline: Joseph moved his family by night
prayer: God, Joseph got up in the middle of the night and moved his family to safety. Through Jesus, the child he protected, make me ready to protect mine at any hour. Keep me alert and close enough to hear You.
reading: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you, for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.” And he rose and took the child and his mother by night and departed to Egypt.
in_jesus: Jesus, a child hunted by a king, was kept safe for the day he would give his own life. Christ was protected so that he could be the one who rescues us.
reflect: If your family needed you to lead tonight, would you be ready?
act: Tonight, gather your wife and kids and pray out loud over your household. Ask God to make you ready.

headline: Simeon waited and saw salvation
prayer: Lord, Simeon waited his whole life, and he held Jesus in his arms. I'm waiting on You for some things too. Let me see Your salvation in Christ, and give me peace while I wait.
reading: Lord, now you are letting your servant depart in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation.
in_jesus: Simeon held Jesus and called him God's salvation. Christ is the answer to the deepest waiting, and he is faithful on every promise still unfulfilled.
reflect: What are you waiting on God for, and are you waiting with peace or with grumbling?
act: Tell one brother today what you are waiting on. Ask him to pray that you would wait with peace.

headline: God sent His Son right on time
prayer: Father, You sent Your Son at exactly the right time, not a minute early or late. I've been impatient with Your timing. Because of Jesus I'm Your son, so help me surrender my timeline and trust Yours.
reading: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
in_jesus: Jesus was born under the law to redeem those under it, so that we receive adoption as sons. Christ came on God's schedule, and he brings us into the family.
reflect: Where are you pushing God to move faster than He is?
act: Pick one deadline you've been forcing and hand it to God in prayer before lunch. Tell your wife or a brother which one.

headline: Peace the world can't give
prayer: Jesus, You give peace the world can't. I need it in the holiday chaos: family tension, money, travel. Calm my heart before I react to anything today. I'm not asking for an easier day, just for You in this one.
reading: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid.
in_jesus: Jesus made peace with God for us through his cross, and he leaves his peace with us. Christ's peace does not depend on a calm house or a full bank account.
reflect: What holiday pressure has your heart troubled, and who is it leaking onto?
act: Take a ten-minute walk before the busiest part of your day and pray. Then ask a stressed coworker or neighbor how he's doing, and tell him where your peace comes from.

headline: Clear the Road for the King
prayer: Lord Jesus, prepare the way in my heart. Straighten the crooked places and clear out what's in the way. Show me what to clear. I want to be ready for You this Christmas, not just ready for company.
reading: A voice cries: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
in_jesus: John the Baptist cleared the road for Jesus, the Lord himself. Christ does not ask us to fix ourselves first. He comes to the one who repents and makes the crooked straight.
reflect: What is sitting in the road between you and Jesus right now?
act: Name the one obstacle and deal with it before Christmas Eve. If it's a person, call him today.

headline: Hand Jesus the heavy end
prayer: Jesus, I'm tired. It's been a long year, and I've carried a lot. I'm coming to You like You told me to. Take the heavy end and give me rest for my soul tonight, even before the year is over.
reading: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
in_jesus: Jesus is gentle and lowly in heart, and he carries what crushes us. Christ took our heaviest burden, sin, to the cross so that we could rest.
reflect: What have you been carrying alone that Jesus has already offered to carry?
act: Tell Jesus your heaviest burden by name this morning. Tonight, be in bed by 10 and leave it with him.

headline: Light breaks into darkness
prayer: Jesus, Light of the world, shine in my darkness and in the darkness of the people around me. Christmas isn't happy for everyone. Holy Spirit, show me who's hurting, and send me to them today.
reading: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who dwelt in a land of deep darkness, on them has light shone.
in_jesus: Jesus is the great light that shone on people in deep darkness. Christ stepped into our grief and loneliness himself, and the darkness has not put his light out.
reflect: Who around you is walking through a dark Christmas this year?
act: Call or visit one lonely or grieving person before Christmas Day. Ask the Spirit for the words, then listen more than you talk.

headline: Immanuel. God with us.
prayer: Immanuel, God with us. God with me. You didn't send a message, You came Yourself. Jesus, thank You. Let my family feel Your presence in our home today, and let this morning be about You.
reading: “Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Immanuel” (which means, God with us).
in_jesus: Jesus is Immanuel. God did not send a message from a distance. Christ came himself, lived among us, died for us, and promised to be with us always.
reflect: Do you live like God is actually with you in your own house?
act: Before opening gifts, gather your family and read Luke 2:1-20 aloud. Then let each person say one thing about Jesus they are thankful for.

headline: He came once. He's coming back.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You came once as a baby, and You're coming back as King. Help me live waiting for You. Find me faithful, awake, and ready whenever that day comes. No more putting off what matters.
reading: Waiting for our blessed hope, the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.
in_jesus: Jesus is our great God and Savior, and he will appear in glory. Christ paid for us at the cross, so we wait for him with hope instead of fear.
reflect: If Jesus returned tonight, what would you wish you had already said or done?
act: Do that one thing today. Make the call, say the apology, or start the conversation you've been avoiding.

headline: The baby is King of Kings
prayer: King of kings and Lord of lords, I bow to You. The baby in the manger rules over everything. Jesus, rule every part of me, including the area I've kept for myself. I stop negotiating today.
reading: On his robe and on his thigh he has a name written, King of kings and Lord of lords.
in_jesus: Jesus is the baby in the manger and the King of kings. Christ won his throne by dying for his enemies, and he rules with that same love.
reflect: Is Jesus King over every part of your life, or only the parts you've handed over?
act: Name the one area you've kept for yourself, like money, a habit, or a relationship. Tell a brother today, and surrender it to Jesus out loud.

headline: Plan your year, let Him steer
prayer: Lord, a new year is coming. I'll make my plans, but You direct my steps. Jesus, be Lord over my goals for faith and health. Keep me humble enough to adjust. I don't want a plan for next year that leaves You out, or one I can't give back to You.
reading: The heart of man plans his way, but the LORD establishes his steps.
in_jesus: Jesus prayed not my will, but yours be done, and walked the Father's path to the cross. Christ is the Lord who directs our steps and goes with us.
reflect: Who is shaping your goals for next year, you or Jesus?
act: Write one faith goal and one health goal for next year. Then share both with a younger man or a coworker and invite him to set one with you.

headline: Everything new. Pain ends.
prayer: Father, thank You for the day when all pain ends. No more tears, no more aging, no more death. Because Jesus rose, I have that hope. Let it shape how I live, train, and love right now.
reading: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away. And he who was seated on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” Also he said, “Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.”
in_jesus: Jesus rose as the firstfruits of the new creation. Christ's empty tomb is the down payment on the day he makes all things new.
reflect: Does the promise of a world with no pain change how you live today?
act: Text or visit one hurting person today. Tell him the hope you have because Jesus rose.

headline: Pass the story on
prayer: Lord, one generation tells the next what You've done. Don't let Your story stop with me. Give me the words and the courage to pass Jesus on to my kids and the younger men around me.
reading: One generation shall commend your works to another, and shall declare your mighty acts.
in_jesus: Jesus is the mighty act every generation needs to hear about: God coming, dying, and rising for sinners. Christ is the story worth passing on.
reflect: What did Jesus do in your life this year that your kids need to hear?
act: Tonight, tell your kids or a younger man one specific thing God did for you this year. Say it face to face.

headline: Finish the Year in Christ
prayer: Jesus, thank You for this year. Every win, every loss, every lesson. I want to fight the good fight, finish the race, and keep the faith. Holy Spirit, help me finish strong and start the new year with You.
reading: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
in_jesus: Jesus finished the work the Father gave him, and he said it is finished. Christ's righteousness covers our year, failures included, so we finish in him, not on our record.
reflect: Where did you fight, finish, and keep the faith this year, and where did you need grace?
act: Write down one win, one failure, and one lesson from this year. Thank Jesus for his grace over each, and send the list to a brother.
